Girard's paradox is avoided because our sorts are not closed under a $Π$-former: function types are placed in sorts according to their rank. Turns out that this system has a unique set of characteristics: it has similar normalization behaviour as STLC (so complexity of normalization is TOWER-complete) while at the same time allowing non-uniform representation of arbitrary elementary recursive functions; furthermore, it has a nontrivial set-theoretical model in ZF+GCH and allows to carry out nontrivial proof developments. Base normalization proof is surprisingly simple (modulo general metatheoretical properties of pure type systems) and has been fully formalized in vanilla Rocq (formerly Coq) without additional axioms.

papers.title: Dual-Slot: From Serial Loops to Parallel Slots in Language Models
papers.abstract: Looped language models increase computational depth by repeatedly applying shared layers, offering a way to improve model quality without adding parameters. However, sequential dependencies between loop iterations increase autoregressive decoding latency. We introduce Dual-Slot, an architecture that reorganizes serial looped computation into parallel latent and prediction slots. Rather than waiting for the current token's latent computation to finish, the prediction slot combines the previous token's deep latent state with the current representation, while the latent slot produces a state for the next decoding step. This shifts the latent dependency across adjacent tokens, replacing two sequential module invocations with a single paired invocation while preserving standard autoregressive generation. To preserve token-level parallelism during training, we use a small number of Jacobi iterations to refine latent states across the sequence in parallel. Experiments on Qwen-style dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models show consistent improvements in language modeling and average downstream accuracy. On the 1B dense model, Dual-Slot reduces Pile validation perplexity from 7.25 to 7.00 and improves average five-shot accuracy across nine task configurations by 2.26 percentage points. After supervised fine-tuning, it improves zero-shot GSM8K accuracy by 5.83 and 3.49 percentage points for the 1B dense and A0.6B MoE models, respectively. Across the evaluated batch sizes, Dual-Slot retains 93.1-96.5% of vanilla decoding throughput for the dense model and 98.1-99.6% for the MoE model.

papers.title: Beyond Factual Accuracy: A Benchmark for Evaluating Perspective Alignment in LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models often generate factually correct responses that fail to maintain user-requested perspectives, blending multiple perspectives and forcing users to filter through unwanted information---a perspective control failure that factual accuracy metrics cannot detect. We introduce PerspectiveBench, a benchmark quantifying perspective alignment by constructing scenarios where multiple valid reasoning paths coexist, and propose the Perspective Alignment Score (PAS) to measure adherence to specified perspectives. Experiments reveal that state-of-the-art models successfully include target content but fail to exclude non-requested perspectives. Providing documents through RAG improves factual grounding but does not resolve perspective drift, as models prioritize comprehensive coverage over strict user constraints. Code and data are available at https://github.com/sunghoon014/PerspectiveBench.

papers.title: On the isoperimetric profile in infinite dimensional pro-Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nontrivial compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric. On the compact pro-Lie group $K^{\N}$ we define a weighted variation by summing the distributional variations in its Lie group coordinates. We prove that all sublevel sets with bounded $L^1$-norm and weighted variation are compact in $L^1$ if and only if the coordinate weights tend to infinity. The proof gives a quantitative estimate for approximation by Haar averages over normal subgroups, illustrating that it is possible to apply a methodology which is typical of the geometric measure theory in a specific area of the topological group theory. The resulting perimeter is invariant under left and right translations and is preserved under pullback by quotient homomorphisms equipped with quotient metrics. Isoperimetric minimizers exist at every prescribed Haar probability. For the infinite torus, the compactness condition is equivalent to properness of a weighted length on its character group and to compactness of a Fourier multiplier's resolvent. Finally, we show that locally compact noncompact groups require an additional condition of tightness, in order to be treated as an appropriate generalization of the compact case.

papers.title: DAGLoop: Aligning Method Design with Experimental Feedback in Automated AI Research
papers.abstract: Automated AI research agents aim to improve machine learning methods by iteratively proposing, implementing, and evaluating candidate methods. Existing work uses the outcome of each evaluation to determine how the next candidate should be revised for performance improvement. However, a candidate often combines multiple design decisions, and its overall outcome alone does not reveal which decisions produced their expected effects, whether their required conditions were satisfied, or which decisions should be retained or revised. Inspired by ablation studies in the machine learning community, we propose DAGLoop to test the expected effect of a design decision by comparing implementations with and without that decision while preserving the other decisions it requires. Specifically, DAGLoop translates each design decision's rationale into a testable expectation and pairs it with a targeted experiment, forming an experimental specification for assessing the expected effect under its required conditions. Using these specifications, we formulate ablation planning as the construction of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) from the candidate method's design: nodes associate decisions with tests, and edges encode dependencies. The DAG specifies which decisions each experiment must retain and supports joint tests when an expected effect requires several decisions to act together. Outcomes are recorded with the tested decisions, expectations, and conditions to form structured research memory. This memory guides the agent in retaining experimentally supported decisions, revising unsupported ones, and planning further experiments when the evidence is unresolved. Experiments on dozens of research tasks demonstrate substantial performance improvements achieved by DAGLoop across diverse executable research settings. Code and evaluation scripts are available at https://github.com/deng34567/DAGLoop.

papers.title: Think Visually Across Space and Time: Grounded Reasoning for Video Segmentation
papers.abstract: Video Reasoning Segmentation (VRS) requires a model to identify an implicitly described target and predict its pixel-level mask trajectory, while resolving the spatial relations and temporal events that determine the answer. Text-only Chain-of-Thought (CoT) can explain a target choice without making the underlying visual references explicit, leaving a \emph{video reference gap} between linguistic inference and the evidence distributed across frames. We introduce \textbf{Temporal Chain of Video Primitives (TCoVP)}, a spatiotemporally grounded form of Video CoT that organizes query-relevant observations into a chronological reasoning chain. Each primitive associates an entity reference with temporal support and timestamped spatial evidence, and the chain interleaves these references with language to guide reasoning about which entity is relevant, when the queried event holds, and where its evidence appears. The selected target primitives then provide box prompts and temporal support for video mask prediction. We construct TCoVP-SFT-15k and TCoVP-RL-13k to learn this representation through supervised fine-tuning and chain-aligned reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments across five VRS benchmarks and three model backbones demonstrate the strong performance of TCoVP, highlighting the effectiveness of organizing spatial and temporal evidence within the reasoning process. All models and code will be publicly released. Project page: \url{https://victor-wjw.github.io/TCoVP/}

papers.title: Summary of Aspen discussions on perturbative uncertainties beyond 7-point variations
papers.abstract: This writeup elaborates on constructive discussions which took place at the Aspen Center for Physics, Aug - Sep 2024, during the program "Tightening the gap between scattering amplitudes and events at the LHC at higher orders". Building on already existing theoretical understanding from the study of scattering amplitudes and resummations at higher orders, we suggest to complement standard 7-point renormalisation- and factorisation-scale variations by additional estimates of missing higher-order terms which are known to be present in the perturbative series. We also summarise a recent proposal for at least one way that non-Gaussian theory uncertainties might be treated within a frequentist framework. This may help to provide more robust and comprehensive uncertainty estimates for experimental and phenomenological applications of perturbative calculations.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction-Enabled Sequence-level Policy Optimization for Reasoning Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning improves the reasoning capability of large language models through verifiable rewards for mathematical and coding tasks. In token-level methods such as GRPO, clipping acts on individual token ratios while the reward and advantage apply to a complete response. Recent sequence-level methods align these units but still use fixed clipping bands, whose tail probabilities change as the score distribution evolves. We propose Conformal Prediction-Enabled Sequence-level Policy Optimization (CSPO), which adaptively calibrates sequence-level clipping bounds using recent training statistics. The resulting band targets a specified marginal tail budget and adapts to policy drift; calibration conditional on response length requires additional assumptions. We bound the probability that a fresh score falls outside the band by the target miscoverage level plus explicit CDF discrepancy and drift terms. Under additional moment conditions, this bound also controls the objective and gradient error relative to the unclipped GSPO power surrogate. Experiments with the Qwen3-1.7B series show improvements over GSPO on difficult mathematical reasoning benchmarks and ALFWorld, with clipping endpoints that adapt during training.

papers.title: A Simulation-Driven Digital Workflow Integrating Bayesian Optimization for Early-Stage Process Design: A Methyl Acetate Production Case Study
papers.abstract: Methyl acetate production via direct carbonylation of dimethyl ether and carbon monoxide involves strong nonlinear interactions among reactor operation, recycle structure, and energy consumption, making conventional simulation-based optimization computationally demanding. In this work, a data-driven framework integrating steady-state process simulation, surrogate modeling, and Bayesian optimization was developed for process intensification. A dataset of 2730 steady-state simulations was generated using a Python-based automated process simulation workflow and a structured design of experiments across the operating domain. Surrogate models were trained to predict carbon conversion yield (C-yield) and cost of specific energy consumption (C-SEC), with neural network-based models showing the best predictive performance and robustness. These models were integrated into a multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework to identify optimal operating regions. Results indicate that high C-yield (up to ~95%) can be achieved with reduced energy cost through lower recycle flow rates and compression demand. Pareto analysis revealed a nonlinear trade-off between C-yield and C-SEC, where further improvements near the conversion limit require disproportionately higher energy input. Validation against rigorous simulations showed deviations below 3% for C-yield and 10% for C-SEC.

papers.title: Structure-Aligned History Learning with Subspace-Structured Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation constructs semantic IDs for catalog items and predicts the next ID from user interaction histories. However, existing methods face limitations in both stages. First, conventional quantizers may produce imbalanced code assignments and lack coherent intermediate semantic units between individual tokens and complete items, limiting history reconstruction. Second, recommendation models remain dominated by next-item prediction, treating historical interactions mainly as conditioning context and providing limited supervision for recovering persistent preferences across the historical path, particularly when relevant preference signals are distributed over distant interactions. To address these limitations, Structure-Aligned History Learning (SAHL) reconnects the two stages by using the structure created during quantization directly for history reconstruction. Its Semantic Residual Balanced Quantization (SRBQ) forms a balanced token-subspace-item hierarchy, and SAHL reconstructs history at these same granularities. Predictive entropy prioritizes uncertain transitions, while curriculum optimization progressively shifts training to inference-aligned next-item prediction. On four Amazon Review categories, SAHL improves NDCG@10 by 18.6%-30.0% over RPG and 2.7%-6.0% over strong method MHL. Controlled analyses verify balanced code use, the benefit of following quantizer-defined groups during reconstruction, and dependence on user history. The relevant code is available at https://github.com/CQU-MM-Intelligent-Lab/SAHL.

papers.title: Towards End-to-End Privacy-Preserving AI for Real-Time ECG Monitoring
papers.abstract: Healthcare artificial intelligence is shifting from centralized archives toward distributed pipelines that combine wearables, edge processing, cloud analytics, and multi-institutional learning. In this regime, electrocardiogram (ECG) streams cross multiple trust boundaries, so privacy cannot be reduced to a single transmission control. Existing privacy-enhancing technologies typically secure isolated stages and leave gaps between acquisition, analysis, and institutional collaboration. This doctoral research develops a unified lifecycle framework for end-to-end privacy-preserving ECG AI. Rather than introducing another privacy mechanism, it orchestrates complementary privacy-enhancing technologies across the clinical ECG lifecycle, allocating each mechanism to the trust boundary where its security, computational, and operational properties are most appropriate. Three interoperable modules instantiate the framework: AES with CKKS-based homomorphic statistics for secure monitoring; adaptive chaotic protection for low-latency edge transmission; and federated learning with homomorphic aggregation under heterogeneous partitions. Across prototype monitoring, signal-security analysis, and simulated collaboration, the programme shows that privacy layers can be composed without collapsing diagnostic utility, while exposing overhead and fidelity limits that constrain clinical translation.

papers.title: Refined proper descent for left completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces
papers.abstract: We refine the proper descent of Postnikov completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces to the dualizable world.

papers.title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources
papers.abstract: Enterprise retail workflows require agents to chain evidence across heterogeneous sources, from structured product and order records to unstructured inquiries and reviews, yet existing agentic RAG benchmarks rarely capture this challenge. To enable controlled evaluation of such workflows, we introduce RetailBridge, a compositional retail benchmark built from persona-driven simulations. Its questions are constructed by linking entities and intermediate answers across heterogeneous sources, requiring agents to identify the relevant sources, carry evidence between them, and produce a grounded answer. To systematically evaluate LLMs on these retail workflows, we develop RetailRAG, a retail-aware framework equipped with auto-schema briefing, source-routed plan chaining, and diagnostic plan revision. RetailRAG consistently outperforms existing agentic RAG baselines across all evaluation axes, serving as a strong reference system for assessing LLM agents on retail workflows. On RetailBridge, evaluating ten LLM backbones with RetailRAG reveals multi-source chaining as the dominant bottleneck across providers and model scales, suggesting that reliable retail agents require explicit cross-source orchestration rather than scaling alone. Code and data are publicly available at \url{https://github.com/DISL-Lab/RetailBridge}.

papers.title: Destinies of Plasmoids Formed from the Magnetic Reconnection Occurring within the Ergo Region of a Rotating Black Hole
papers.abstract: It is widely accepted that magnetic reconnections occur successively in black hole accretion flows, especially on the equatorial plane, owing to the formation of the equatorial current sheet. When magnetic reconnection takes place within the ergosphere of a rotating black hole, one of the ejected plasmoids (denoted as $p_-$) may acquire negative energy-at-infinity density, while the companion plasmoid (denoted as $p_+$) correspondingly carries the energy extracted from the black hole. This mechanism, known as the Comisso-Asenjo process, provides a viable astrophysical pathway for extracting energy from a rotating black hole. Generally speaking, two conditions have to be satisfied for successful energy extraction. First, $p_-$ is generated via magnetic reconnection with negative energy-at-infinity density. Second, the associated $p_+$, which carries the extracted energy, must escape to infinity. Though a number of studies have promoted the theory of the Comisso-Asenjo process, the escape of $p_+$ lacks consideration. In this work, we adopt geodesic approach to systematically examine the destinies of $p_+$ after ejection, thereby establishing the complete conditions for energy extraction from a rotating black hole via magnetic reconnection. We redefine the covering factor, for which only escaping $p_+$ are counted. This quantity reflects how probable the successful energy extraction occurs in an accretion system. Through analysis of this revised covering factor, we identify a lower bound on the black hole spin, $a=0.8005$, below which energy extraction via magnetic reconnection can never succeed, no matter how high the magnetization of the bulk plasma is. This limit suggests that the spin-down of a black hole caused by successive magnetic reconnections would terminate once the spin decreases to approximately 0.8005.

papers.title: From Zero to OCR: A Data-Centric Framework for Unsupported Low-Resource Scripts
papers.abstract: Optical character recognition (OCR) remains inaccessible to many low-resource scripts because annotated document images are unavailable and synthetic training data can fail to preserve script-specific visual structure. We present a data-centric framework that builds end-to-end OCR for such scripts from only an unannotated text corpus and digital fonts, without manually annotating a single training image. A synthetic data engine renders word, line and page images with correct complex-script shaping and automatically derived labels; a YOLOv8 word detector and a convolutional recurrent recognizer trained with connectionist temporal classification learn from these images; and a stage-gate evaluation protocol isolates recognition error before detection is introduced. We demonstrate the framework on Kashmiri, a Perso-Arabic Nastaliq script with approximately 6.8 million speakers that none of six widely used OCR engines supports. Three line-level recognizers, including one transferred from Arabic, stalled between 41% and 79% character error rate (CER), motivating a word-level formulation; subsequent improvements came primarily from rendering fidelity, diacritic-preserving crop margins and tuned non-maximum suppression. The resulting system achieves 0.39% CER on held-out words, 10.0% on synthetic pages and 13.5% on browser-rendered digital pages, and establishes reference results of 18.45% on typeset book pages and 49.8% on degraded historical documents. We publicly release the trained models, the inference code and a synthetic dataset of 285,864 Kashmiri text-line images, and we describe a step-by-step procedure for building OCR for other unsupported scripts.

papers.title: Pre-Query Retention with Bounded Bit and Word Retrieval
papers.abstract: An agent can retain information before receiving a future question and later retrieve evidence from an archive. Evaluating this arrangement requires accounting for both retained information and the width of each retrieval response. Decision-tree capacity bounds describe individual sets of distinguishable records, but a memory writer must encode every possible record before the query is known. We study fixed-length retention beside an immutable binary archive, with a worst-case limit on raw bit or word reads. We characterize feasible one-bit-read memory cells and construct encoders that partition the complete record space. Supporting pairwise exclusive disjunction and conjunction with one bit read is equivalent to supporting every Boolean query. For multiple reads, we combine explicit encoders with decision-tree counting and an entropy converse. The word-read bounds differ by at most two retained bits when the read budget is at most half the archive length. Under an explicit condition on word width and archive length, raw-word caching attains the exact optimum among all writers. A related condition preserves this optimum under positive average error. Exhaustive checks validate the implementations. In a matched dialogue-agent study, a categorical sufficient statistic preserves source decisions with less storage and lower decoding latency than the universal encoder. A catalogue-specific index reduces private state further and requires additional shared storage. The results characterize how response width and future query structure determine retention requirements.

papers.title: Identity crisis on tightly $C^{(2)}$-compact cardinals
papers.abstract: Bagaria and Goldberg asked if $κ$ being tightly $C^{(n)}$-compact implies $κ\in C^{(n+1)}$ for natural numbers $n\ge 1$? Usuba gave a negative answer for $n=1$. In this paper we give a negative answer for $n=2$.

papers.title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models need effective ways to acquire and use external knowledge beyond what they retain from pretraining. Continued pretraining risks catastrophic forgetting, while retrieval at inference time can add substantial overhead. External parametric memory avoids online retrieval, but constructing its training data requires extensive offline search, and output-level interpolation provides only shallow fusion. We introduce Deep Fusion Memory (DFM), a parametric memory architecture that reduces this construction workload and incorporates learned memory into intermediate hidden states. A causal memory predictor learns to generate memory from the preceding context, using retrieved chunk embeddings from the corpus as supervision. The predicted memory is shared across tokens within each chunk and fused into their hidden states through gated cross-attention. Memory prediction and fusion are trained end to end with the backbone frozen, and inference requires no explicit retrieval. Compared with existing parametric memory approaches, which often construct token-level memory targets, DFM requires $32\times$ fewer retrieval queries and $2048\times$ fewer retrieved items to construct its training data. Across six QA tasks, DFM performs better over the strongest baseline by 12.71% on Mistral-7B-v0.3 and 11.19% on Qwen3-8B-Base. Beyond QA, domain adaptation yields average gains of 6.51 and 4.38 points over Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base, respectively.

papers.title: The center conjecture for cyclotomic Hecke algebras and cohomology of quiver varieties
papers.abstract: For a quiver without edge loops, we construct an isomorphism from the cohomology of a Nakajima quiver variety with coefficients in an arbitrary field to the Jucys--Murphy center of the corresponding cyclotomic KLR algebra over that field. In affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, combining this with a dimension count shows that this Jucys--Murphy center coincides with the full center in characteristic $0$, when the characteristic does not divide $e$, and when the characteristic equals $e$. This follows from a geometric theorem showing that the sum of these cohomology rings is cocyclic as a module over an integral form of a loop algebra. As a consequence, we prove that the center of a cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type $G(r,1,n)$ with $q\neq 1$ over any field is generated by symmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements, and the same holds over any commutative domain in which $q-1$ is invertible. We also prove a generalization to the integral case of the conjecture of Krylov, Paegelow and Shlykov identifying the equivariant $K$-theory of the core of a Gieseker variety with the cocenter of the generic cyclotomic Hecke algebra, including the natural extension of this conjecture to positive characteristic.

papers.title: Large exchange bias from coupled antiferromagnetic order and glassy magnetic freezing in $Co_{0.36}NbS_{2}$
papers.abstract: Magnetization measurements on single-crystalline $Co_{0.36}NbS_{2}$ reveal antiferromagnetic order near $T_{N} \simeq 26 K$ and a lower-temperature history-dependent magnetic response consistent with glassy freezing of a subset of magnetic moments. After field cooling, $M(H)$ loops exhibit a sizable exchange-bias shift, reaching $|H_{EB}| \simeq 4.4 kOe$ at $1.8 K$ for a $70 kOe$ field-cooling sweep protocol. The training effect, field-sweep and cooling-field protocol dependence, and disappearance of the bias near a blocking temperature $T_{B} \simeq 12 K$, well below $T_{N}$, support an interpretation in which frozen uncompensated moments are exchange-coupled to an antiferromagnetic matrix. These results suggest that antiferromagnetic-glassy-moment coupling may provide a broader route to exchange bias in off-stoichiometric magnetic $NbS_{2}$ intercalates.

papers.title: The Ericson Transition in Time-Reversal Invariant Systems: Orthogonally Invariant Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: We investigate the distributions of off-diagonal scattering matrix elements and cross-sections in the Ericson regime for systems that are time-reversal and rotationally invariant. In previous works, we developed techniques to analyze the Ericson transition by means of asymptotic expansions in the cases of unitarily and symplectically invariant Hamiltonians. Here, we prove that Gaussian and exponential behavior is found as the leading-order term of an asymptotic expansion of those distributions also in the orthogonal case, which is often the relevant one for analyzing experiments. Moreover, we derive the subleading-order term and compare with numerical simulations. Finally, we discuss similarities and differences of the Ericson transition for all three Wigner-Dyson classes.

papers.title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D
papers.abstract: Despite having an asymptotically optimal rate of convergence on convex quadratics, the acceleration of Polyak's heavy-ball method and a characterization of its dynamics within more general settings have remained long standing open problems. Recently, the work of Goujaud et al. [Math. Program. (2025)] made progress regarding acceleration in the context of smooth, strongly convex minimization: for a small enough inverse condition number, either the method does not accelerate on quadratics, or there exists a smooth strongly convex function such that heavy-ball cycles over the roots of unity. The constructed functions have two variables, thus leaving the question of acceleration over univariate functions open. In this work, we use a Fourier-based analysis to i) provide a proof for the non-acceleration of the heavy-ball method over the class of univariate smooth strongly convex functions. We also ii) provide a strict enlargement of the previous root-of-unity cycling region, with insights regarding the "fractional" sets of Goujaud et al. [arXiv:2502.19916], and iii) give a higher dimensional cycling instance which is not covered by root-of-unity cycling.

papers.title: Generative marginal learning for finite-size molecular simulation with application to stress calculation
papers.abstract: We propose generative marginal learning (GML), a framework for equilibrium sampling and local observable estimation in molecular simulations. By training a conditional diffusion model on large-system simulations, GML learns the marginal distribution of a retained region, enabling configuration generation without explicitly simulating the surrounding environment or imposing periodic boundary conditions on the retained region. We derive a marginal effective potential and the associated conditional mean-force identity, which provide the basis for both denoising and force-alignment training. As an application, we estimate the spatially averaged Irving--Kirkwood stress near a vacancy defect. Numerical tests on a two-dimensional Lennard--Jones crystal and three-dimensional BCC Fe under combined tension and shear demonstrate improved local stress accuracy relative to small periodic molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Lucas recurrences and Lambert series in coprime double sums
papers.abstract: For the Lucas numbers $L_0=2$, $L_1=1$, and $L_n=L_{n-1}+L_{n-2}$, we obtain \[ \sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}}\frac{1}{L_{2n}L_{2m}L_{2(n+m)}}=\frac1{45}. \] This follows from the absolutely convergent identity \[ \sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}}\frac{q^{n+m}} {(1+q^n)(1+q^m)(1+q^{n+m})} =\frac{q^2}{(1-q^2)^2},\qquad |q|<1. \] We give a self-contained proof by local cancellation on the Calkin--Wilf tree, as a specialization of Hata's Farey-interval telescoping principle. Specializations yield a hyperbolic-cosine identity \[\sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}} \frac{1}{\cosh(nx)\cosh(mx)\cosh((n+m)x)} =\frac{2}{\sinh^2(2x)}, x>0\] and weighted sums for canonical second-order Lucas recurrences. Decomposing arbitrary positive pairs according to their greatest common divisor gives an unrestricted sum expressed by a Lambert series and the quasimodular Eisenstein series $E_2$. Conversely, Möbius inversion recovers the primitive identity from a double Lambert-series result of Cui, Kumar, and Singh.

papers.title: A Novel OFDM-FMCW Waveform for Low-Complexity Joint Sensing and Communication
papers.abstract: With the advent of 6th Generation (6G) wireless networks, integrating Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) waveforms presents a promising solution for simultaneous communication and sensing. While OFDM offers high communication performance, it requires complex transceivers for sensing applications. Conversely, FMCW is easily implemented for sensing but provides low data rates for communication. This letter derives the mathematical relationship between OFDM and FMCW, showing how FMCW can be generated from the diagonal elements of the OFDM modulator (\ie, the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) matrix). We propose a novel approach that leverages the DFT matrix to seamlessly integrate these two waveforms, minimizing interference and enabling high data rate communication alongside low-complexity sensing receiver design. Extensive simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique in achieving simultaneous sensing and

papers.title: Generation-Heavy Hybrid Machine Translation
papers.abstract: The state of the art techniques in Machine Translation (MT) require large amounts of symmetric resources from source and target languages. This is true regardless of whether the approach is Transfer or Interlingua, Symbolic or Statistical. Symmetry within these approaches is necessary to ensure quality, robustness and retargetability. In reality, such symmetry, whether it is in terms of structural transfer lexicons, interlingual dictionaries or parallel corpora, is a major bottleneck in developing any MT system. This dissertation presents an approach to MT that addresses the lack of symmetry by exploiting symbolic and statistical target language resources in source-poor/target-rich language pairs. This approach is called Generation-Heavy Hybrid Machine Translation (GHMT). Expected source language resources include a syntactic parser and a simple one-to-many translation dictionary. No transfer rules or complex interlingual representations are used. Rich target language symbolic resources are used to overgenerate multiple structural variations from a target-glossed syntactic dependency representation of source language sentences. Statistical target-language resource are then used to select amongst the overgenerated translations. The source-target asymmetry of systems developed in this approach makes them more easily retargetable to new source languages.

papers.title: Which Code Changes Need Re-embedding? CIPBench and the Limits of Multi-Signal Index Maintenance
papers.abstract: Repository-level retrieval-augmented generation systems must keep vector indexes synchronized with continuously evolving code, yet there is no principled basis for deciding which changed code units actually need new embeddings. We ask whether the retrieval impact of a code change can be anticipated before that embedding is computed. Across 10 open-source repositories in Python, Go, and JavaScript, we characterize how a change propagates from syntactic substantiality through embedding displacement to retrieval impact. The links are informative but not deterministic: syntactic class separates displacement sharply, yet impact depends on a unit's retrieval exposure as much as on how far its representation moves, and recurring counterexamples bound what any single signal can decide. We formalize the decision as CIPBench, a benchmark that scores maintenance policies under a strict pre-embedding information boundary. Prediction works, and one signal exhausts it. A ranker using only a unit's change history substantially reduces retrieval harm relative to random and recency-based scheduling. Combining it with three further signals--individually discriminative and largely unassociated with one another--leaves the decision statistically unchanged across every budget we evaluate, for reasons we trace to the structure of the score rather than to its tuning. What pays off is not ranking but filtering: units whose text is unchanged from the indexed state can be skipped with no risk and, in the most reversion-heavy project, at nearly half the embedding cost. Signal-level informativeness is therefore not evidence of decision-level value, and separating the two requires evaluating the decision a signal produces rather than its association with the outcome.

papers.title: Annealing Dynamics of the Two-Dimensional Fully Frustrated Ising Model
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical scaling properties of the two-dimensional fully frustrated Ising model by simulated annealing. The model has a highly degenerate, critical ground state with well known equilibrium properties. To study its out-of-equilibrium behavior, we develop an annealing protocol that is convenient for extending the Kibble-Zurek mechanism to the case of an exponentially divergent correlation length in the limit of the temperature $T \to T_c = 0$. We find excellent agreement with the scaling forms derived, including a dependence on the initial temperature that is not present in the conventional Kibble-Zurek mechanism. The dynamic exponent $z$ is consistent among all quantities studied; fits of its dependence on the initial temperature give $z = 1.99(2)$ (susceptibility), $z = 2.072(8)$ (excess energy), and $z = 2.09(3)$ (Edwards-Anderson order parameter). These values are close to $z=2$, which is consistent with previous studies of relaxation after instantaneous quenches and of time dependent correlations in equilibrium, including the estimate $z = 2.004(9)$ from equilibrium autocorrelation functions.

papers.title: A new regime of the C-metric: Super accelerating black holes
papers.abstract: We define and investigate the super accelerating regime of the charged C-metric, which arises at large acceleration. In this regime, the polar coordinate must be restricted to a smaller interval within $(0,π)$, and the resulting boundary defines a new axis of symmetry. This changes the conical singularity structure of the spacetime and, consequently, its string/strut interpretation. We further show that, when the conical defect at the south pole is removed, the Komar mass takes the simple form $M_K=1/(4A)$, up to the normalization of the time translation Killing vector. Finally, we explore the near extremal limits of this regime, identifying new limiting geometries.

papers.title: GenAI as an 'Invisible Hand' in Opinion Dynamics: Evidence from a Group-Level Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Recent arguments suggest that genAI can act as an invisible hand that gradually shapes social structures, such as collective beliefs and norms. The argument is that if millions of people repeatedly consult genAI tools, their generated outcomes quietly shape what becomes acceptable, reasonable or conventional. We study this in the context of collective opinion dynamics, i.e., how groups form opinions around controversial dynamics. We present the findings of a simulation including 50,000 group discussions across 50 controversial statements, three LLMs, and different social configurations. We vary two characteristics of LLM interaction-agreeableness and personalization-and compare the influence of genAI in homogeneous and heterogeneous groups. Our findings indicate that profile-specific personalization increases LLM influence when models adopt a non-neutral stance, i.e., when they agree or disagree with the user. Furthermore, we find that neutral LLMs have a stronger effect in homogeneous groups. Based on our simulation, we generate a set of hypotheses to specify how, why and when AI-related features and social configurations jointly shape collective opinion making.

papers.title: Explore or Confirm? LLM Agents Misallocate Measurements Under Noise
papers.abstract: As model reasoning gets cheaper, the physical experiment becomes the slow and costly step in discovery. Each experiment returns a noisy reading: a high value can mean a good candidate or a lucky draw. With a fixed budget, an AI agent must keep choosing between exploring a new candidate and confirming a promising one by re-testing it. We measure that choice in Wellocate, a simulated assay campaign with known true values. It is built on a generated landscape and on two real protein datasets, GB1 and PhoQ, scrambled so no model can answer from memory. We test five language models as minimal agents, with no tools and no memory beyond the history in each prompt. They misallocate in both directions. Three over-confirm, spending most of the budget re-testing. On the generated landscape one under-confirms, trusting single readings, and there every model ends with a worse final pick than a basic scripted strategy. Each failure has its own cause. The over-confirmers run short of new candidates worth trying: a list of untried candidates cuts their re-testing and, on real protein data, makes two of them pick much better. A running summary of their readings or a description of the landscape changes it by at most five percentage points. For the under-confirmer, re-testing its top candidates in a final round, replayed on its own campaigns, recovers only about a quarter of what it loses by picking the wrong candidate. This suggests confirmation has to run through the whole campaign. We release Wellocate as a benchmark and reinforcement-learning environment with frozen splits and scripted baselines. With it, anyone can measure how an agent splits its budget before trusting it with real experiments, and train agents to split it better. Code, data and the environment are available at https://github.com/Xstendyl/wellocate.

papers.title: Frustration-Assisted Electrical Switching in $Co_xTaS_2$
papers.abstract: Electrical switching in antiferromagnets is commonly described as the action of current-induced torques on a rigid order parameter. In frustrated magnets, however, competing states can create a history-dependent energy landscape in which slow collective dynamics actively participate in electrical reconfiguration. Here, we demonstrate frustration-assisted switching in near-stoichiometric $Co_xTaS_2$, a van der Waals antiferromagnet located at the composition-sensitive boundary between Hall-active and Hall-inactive multi-Q-related magnetic regimes. Although the crystals exhibit no resolved spontaneous Hall response, they retain van Hove singularities near the Fermi level and order antiferromagnetically below $T_N \simeq 31.5 K$. Current pulses write nonvolatile anisotropic resistance states in microstructured devices, with an activation current density nearly an order of magnitude below that reported for the Hall-active lower-intercalation phase. The switching response separates into two temperature-dependent dynamical regimes rather than following a single current threshold. Independent magnetization-aging and post-field-relaxation measurements reveal slow, history-dependent magnetic dynamics, and the relaxation strength closely follows the inverse switching amplitude. These results identify magnetic frustration and glassy dynamics as central ingredients in the electrical reconfiguration of $Co_xTaS_2$, establishing a route to functional switching through a dynamically soft antiferromagnetic landscape.

papers.title: A learner-free swarm reaches the explore-exploit equilibrium: A self-organized attractor approximating the reinforcement-learning solution
papers.abstract: The explore-exploit trade-off is the core problem of reinforcement learning (RL). In its multi-agent, resource-sharing form the optimum is not a scalar-return maximum but an equilibrium allocation -- the ideal-free distribution (IFD), the Nash equilibrium of a congestion game. We show that a minimal foraging swarm reaches the shape of this equilibrium as a self-organized attractor -- foragers in proportion to resource richness (matching slope 0.94) -- with no learner, no trained parameters, and no payoff or reward read anywhere in its dynamics. Agents explore by heavy-tailed (Levy) flights, recruit neighbours to a discovery through a threshold cascade on their proximity network, and disperse as a patch crowds; removing the coupling of recruitment to movement collapses the matching (slope 0.08). The reinforcement learning is at the level of the problem and the allocation reached, not the micro-rule. The swarm reaches this equilibrium rather than learning it, attaining its shape but not the exact equilibrium: it stays measurably exploitable (Nash-gap 0.58 versus ~0.01 for a converged learner). Against PPO learners (feedforward, centralized-critic, and graph message-passing) trained in the same sensing-limited environment, the reward-free swarm at zero training matches the IFD gradient more faithfully than any learner (slope ~1 vs 0.69-0.91) and ties the best learner's harvest where clustered (both plateau at ~0.80 of an oracle ceiling), while the learner collects more where resource is scarce (0.33 vs 0.22) and holds tighter per-capita intake. Learning thus buys precision and transfer, not a better allocation; neither message passing nor a centralized critic exceeds it at this budget. We read this not as beating RL, but as evidence that a minimal swarm's physics reaches the equilibrium RL seeks without a learner, a reward, or a trained parameter. A companion paper develops the mechanism.

papers.title: Compile Once, Run Cheap: Frozen, Portable Skills for Embodied Agents, and What Recursive Self-Improvement Adds
papers.abstract: Embodied AI lacks the data-rich pretraining that gave language models their agents and skills, so new manipulation capability costs demonstrations per task or a frontier model in every episode. We study a third route: a strong general model acts only as an offline author that writes, runs, diagnoses and repairs a manipulation skill in simulation until it passes an exam on layouts drawn after freezing; the frozen skill then runs as code alone or under a cheap caller that reads only its description. We call this skill-level recursive self-improvement Skill-RSI and specify a compile protocol (isolated, audited author; hidden validation layouts; no-feedback and inherit-only controls; tamper-evident ledger) and a reuse protocol that runs the identical files with executors from another model family. On 7 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with cluttered tables, Claude Code compiled 4 tasks into 7 frozen skills, 5 from a first draft needing only qualification, at USD 4.29-8.22 of author cost each (USD 55 per skill counting the 13 failed campaigns). The other three tasks did not compile in 18 campaigns, including five with GPT-6 and a pre-registered 150-layout run: on the hardest task every campaign scored 78-95 of 100 but had 3-16 safety aborts, failing the gate of 95% success with zero aborts; a 100-episode exam bounds an abort rate only to 3.6%. On hidden layouts, repair that inherits the previous version beat from-scratch rewriting in 8 of 8 controlled campaigns (sign test p = 0.004); an inherit-only lineage attributes most of the gap to inheritance, with development feedback adding a little (3 of 3, p = 0.125). Write-once campaigns found no detectable first-draft effect of practice (minimum detectable effect 14 points). The frozen skills kept 148/150 successes on new layouts with no model and 147/150 with a DeepSeek-flash caller at USD 0.00028-0.00054 per episode; no direct-control baseline was run.

papers.title: Sharp Pointwise Error Estimates of Finite Element Methods for the Biharmonic Equation
papers.abstract: We prove sharp pointwise error estimates for finite element approximations of the clamped biharmonic equation on convex polygonal domains. For $C^1$-conforming elements, we establish $W^{2,p}$-stability for all $2\le p\le \infty$, together with best-approximation type estimates in $W^{1,\infty}$ and $L^\infty$. For the nonconforming Morley element, we derive optimal estimates in $W^{2,p}$, $W^{1,\infty}$, and $L^\infty$; in particular, the $L^\infty$-error is of order $O(h^2)$ without an additional logarithmic factor. The analysis is based on three ingredients: local energy estimates for conforming and nonconforming plate elements, a removal of the local $L^2$-error term in these estimates, and Hölder estimates for derivatives of the Green's function. These tools are combined with a dyadic decomposition argument for regularized Green's functions. The results remove logarithmic losses present in earlier pointwise estimates for fourth-order problems and yield sharp rates for classical plate elements such as the Argyris, Bogner--Fox--Schmit (BFS), Hsieh--Clough--Tocher (HCT), and Morley elements.

papers.title: Polynomial Learning of Positive ReLU Networks under Gaussian Inputs
papers.abstract: We study positive, bias-free, one-hidden-layer ReLU networks under standard Gaussian inputs. We obtain algorithms with polynomial sample and real-arithmetic complexity, without separation or conditioning assumptions on the hidden directions. When the conditional label mean is a width-$k$ network with total output weight at most one, the learner achieves squared prediction error $\varepsilon$ with output width at most $k+\min\{k,d\}$ and complexity linear in one plus the residual second moment. For arbitrary labels with bounded second moment, we obtain a positive ReLU network of width $O(k\log(2/\varepsilon))$. Its risk is bounded by the irreducible noise variance plus $Ck^3\log^{9/2}(2k/\varepsilon)$ times the squared distance of the conditional mean to the target class, plus $\varepsilon$. The proofs combine implicit Hermite moments, orthogonal tensor-train compression, and a direction decoder whose probability of returning a direction far from every atom is bounded linearly in the compression and estimation errors. Exact Gaussian localization refines the resulting direction covers. In the agnostic setting, a cone-constrained convex program with a scale-dependent penalty produces a positive network; in the conditional-mean setting, exact sparsification yields the smaller width. We also establish projective direction recovery and confidence amplification with sample complexity proportional to the logarithm of the reciprocal failure probability.

papers.title: MACE: Multigroup-Multiangle Integrated Thermal Compton Scattering Kernel
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive set of accurate Compton-scattering tables for use in multigroup, multiangle radiation-transport calculations. The tables contain the exact thermal Compton kernel integrated over incident-energy groups, scattered-energy groups, and angular bins. To generate them, we develop a deterministic integration method in which the pointwise kernel is evaluated with a robust numerical treatment that remains accurate across challenging regions of parameter space. The multidimensional integrals are computed using nested quadratures whose panels adapt to the Compton recoil ridge, its thermal broadening, and the nearly elastic forward-scattering boundary layer. We validate the tabulated results against published kernel profiles, angular and energy moments, mean free paths, multigroup redistribution data, and an independent Monte Carlo estimator. The resulting tables provide the radiation-transport community with accurate, reproducible, and readily usable Compton redistribution matrices and angular moments.

papers.title: How Much Feedback Is Needed to Break Template Protection? The Geometric Vulnerability of Biometric Authentication
papers.abstract: Biometric authentication systems increasingly use privacy-preserving mechanisms to protect sensitive templates. However, the authentication interface itself may still leak information that enables reconstruction attacks. Prior attacks exploit released similarity scores, whereas more advanced systems reveal only the binary accept/reject decision. This binary feedback provides substantially less information, making template reconstruction far more challenging. In this work, we introduce query-efficient reconstruction attacks under extremely limited feedback, addressing two key limitations of prior attacks. First, we introduce the first attack that reconstructs protected biometric templates using only authentication success/failure feedback by exploiting the geometric constraints of biometric authentication. Second, we introduce distribution-aware query-efficient reconstruction methods for score-releasing systems, achieving a more realistic threat model by reducing the number of required queries by a factor of $5\times$ compared to recent prior score-based attacks. Finally, we combine these two insights by incorporating a pretrained facial diffusion prior into our geometric binary attack, reducing the number of required queries by a factor of $5\times$. Our findings reveal a fundamental security limitation of biometric authentication: independently of the template protection mechanism, the authentication process itself exposes geometric information that can enable perfect template reconstruction up to numerical precision. Moreover, the distribution of biometric templates can be leveraged to make significantly more effective reconstruction attacks.

papers.title: Memory as Belief: Bayesian Evolution of Memory for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory to accumulate past experiences for continual adaptation. However, effectively reusing memory requires accurately assessing its value, as retrieved experiences may become unreliable when transferred across task contexts. Despite its importance, memory valuation remains largely underexplored, with existing methods relying on historical retrieval success rates that overlook the context dependency of memory usefulness and the varying reliability of estimates under different amounts of evidence. Inspired by the Bayesian brain hypothesis, we propose BEAM (Bayesian-style Evolutionary Agentic Memory), a framework that reformulates memory value evaluation as a parameterized cognitive inference process, where memory value is represented as a context-conditioned dynamic belief rather than a passive historical statistic. Specifically, BEAM infers memory value beliefs from current task contexts and continuously calibrates them using execution feedback as empirical evidence, transforming memory from passive storage into an adaptive cognitive mechanism for continual self-evolution. Extensive experiments across reasoning and code generation benchmarks demonstrate that BEAM consistently improves memory utilization and enables continual self-evolution of LLM agents.

papers.title: LC-TSRNet: A Land-Cover-Guided Two-Stage Network for Annual MODIS Surface Reflectance Time Series Reconstruction
papers.abstract: MODIS surface reflectance (SR) products often suffer from data gaps due to cloud contamination and sensor malfunctions, limiting their applications in long-term and large-scale studies. Most existing methods rely on cloud-free observations from optical time series or introduce SAR time series as auxiliary information. However, due to the coarse spatial resolution of MODIS, cloud-free reference images are difficult to obtain, and SAR imagery is not well matched to the spatial resolution of MODIS, making it difficult to provide effective prior constraints. To address these issues, this study proposes LC-TSRNet for seamless reconstruction of annual MODIS SR products. In the first stage, an annual land cover map is introduced as prior knowledge, and CSPM is designed by leveraging the spectral similarity within identical land cover types, thereby providing prior spectral constraints for missing regions. In the second stage, to address large-area, persistent, and overlapping gaps in MODIS imagery, SMRM is designed to adaptively exploit and integrate multi-scale spatiotemporal contextual information. Meanwhile, to address the limited collaborative utilization of spatio-temporal-spectral information, 3DAM is designed to impose cross-dimensional joint constraints. Considering the lack of publicly available MODIS sample datasets, this study constructs the AIRMOD-TSR dataset. Extensive experimental results show that LC-TSRNet outperforms the comparison methods and achieves better reconstruction accuracy and spectral fidelity. Under the spatially adjacent scenario, LC-TSRNet improves PSNR by 0.56 dB and reduces SAM by 0.13°. The vegetation monitoring application further verifies the practical value of the reconstructed SR time series.

papers.title: ClinSDT: LLM-Encoded Clinical Semantic Guidance for Sepsis Treatment via Decision Transformer
papers.abstract: Offline sepsis treatment aims to learn treatment policies from retrospective ICU trajectories. Decision Transformer-based methods provide a natural sequence modeling framework for this task, but they mainly rely on raw physiological states and historical clinician actions. Such raw trajectory tokens may not explicitly capture clinical semantics that clinicians use in practice, such as patient severity, recent treatment response, and current risk priorities. To address this limitation, we propose ClinSDT, an LLM-assisted Decision Transformer framework for offline sepsis treatment. ClinSDT uses a frozen LLM as a semantic bridge rather than a treatment decision maker. It constructs three clinical semantic views from ICU trajectories, namely Profile, Context, and Advisory, and inserts their encoded representations as independent tokens into a Decision Transformer policy. To support policy refinement and rollout, ClinSDT further trains a Treatment-Response Forecaster to estimate the next physiological state, SAPS-II change, and predictive uncertainty from state-action inputs. In the second training stage, the forecaster screens local counterfactual treatment candidates, and only low-uncertainty candidates with lower predicted SAPS-II increase are distilled into the policy after semantic regeneration. During inference, ClinSDT performs closed-loop treatment rollout by refreshing semantic inputs from the currently available patient state. Experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV show that ClinSDT achieves consistent relative improvements over representative imitation learning, offline reinforcement learning, and Decision Transformer baselines under the same rollout protocol. Code and data are available at https://github.com/KAG778/ClinSDT.

papers.title: Behave Like Experts: Fusing Data with Semantic Knowledge for Effective and Efficient Semantic Map Construction
papers.abstract: Semantic map models (SMMs) construct a graph that reflects conceptual similarity by comparing cross-lingual form-meaning mappings. Experts build such models not only by obeying the data constraint, i.e., the connectivity hypothesis, which states that conceptual nodes belonging to the same form must be connected, but also by incorporating their prior semantic knowledge. Current automatic methods ignore this knowledge, which harms both accuracy and efficiency by enlarging the search space of candidate graphs. In this paper, we fuse the distributional semantic knowledge hidden in the internal representations of language models into a top-down, data-driven algorithm. This expert-like behavior re-sorts the candidates in a huge search space, guided by conceptual semantics similarity. Experiments on a self-collected benchmark of 10 datasets and comprehensive metrics show that our method builds SMMs both effectively and efficiently.

papers.title: Memories That Outlive Their Reasons: Dependency-Tethered Memory for Tool-Using LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Agents now act on the Web, publishing packages, models and datasets through registry APIs, and remembering past verifications spares them the work. But a verdict rests on premises. When a signing key is revoked, everything built on it stops passing, yet the advisory names only the key, and the old verdicts of its dependents may never share a retrieval window with it. This non-locality of invalidation turns memory into a liability: in long simulated chats, an agent reading a memory of atomic facts publishes 62% of the objects whose failure lies upstream, each backed by a record that was true when written. Yet derivation is local even when invalidation is not. Tether records, at write time, the exact versions each verdict derives from, and at read time withdraws any verdict whose support has failed anywhere in the store; the agent reads the same fields as before. On Fallout, a generator of versioned worlds with hypothesis-blind simulated histories shared by every memory, Tether publishes 0.3% of upstream-failing objects across three domains when relations are stated with their verdicts, with 37% fewer verification calls than checking everything. A-Mem and Graphiti re-verify most candidates (0.83--0.86 checks per candidate), which limits their savings, yet publish 9% of upstream-failing objects; Mem0 relies on memory more and publishes 42%. Flushing every verdict on any failure is as safe as Tether but costs 32% more checks. The gain over fact memory holds with three open-weight backbones, a whole-store window and real Go advisories. These gains depend on capturing dependencies: when relations arrive in sessions apart from their verdicts, Tether's downstream unsafe publication rate rises to 9.4--22.1%. It also degrades with weaker writers that miss dependencies or invalidation events.

papers.title: Secure Distortion-Aware GNN Precoding under Active Eavesdropping in Cell-Free Networks
papers.abstract: This paper considers a cell-free (CF) network under active eavesdropping. We show that nonlinear power amplifier (PA) distortion, together with the per-access point (AP) large-scale-gain fingerprint of the attack, can be exploited across cooperating APs to enhance physical layer security (PLS). Classical zero-forcing (ZF)-artificial noise (AN) precoders rely on a linear transmitter and an unbiased estimate, and thus cannot exploit either. We propose a distortion aware graph neural network (GNN) precoder that designs the signal beams at cooperating APs and exploits both the PA distortion and the per-AP fingerprint to enhance the secrecy rate, combined with a null-space AN block to form the GNN-AN scheme. The GNN is trained on channel estimates biased by an uplink pilot-spoofing attack to maximise the average per-user secrecy rate. Simulations across different numbers of APs show uniformly higher outage secrecy rates than ZF-AN under attack, reaching gains of 15% at the 1% outage level and 8.9% at the 5% outage level at L = 32 APs, input back-off (IBO) = -1 dB, and attacker-to-targeted user pilot power ratio of 0.5, under the same signal/AN power split.

papers.title: Beyond Policy Discrepancy: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. We propose Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), which combines specialist merging with capability-guided allocation to account for what the student has already learned. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Supervision decreases as capability gaps close and increases when estimated student capability regresses, while dense token-level guidance remains provided by the teachers. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and instruction following, CA-MOPD achieves an average score of 32.22, outperforming naive MOPD, Open-MOPD, and the merged initialization by 0.86, 0.83, and 0.74 points, respectively. Controlled comparisons further support the benefits of merged initialization and capability-gap guidance under matched training budgets.

papers.title: The Bottleneck Is Retrieval, Not Reading: Diagnosing Evidence-Based Generation with RAG for Long Context Question Answering
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is the dominant paradigm for grounding large language models in external corpora, but its similarity-driven, chunked pipeline has structural blind spots: it cannot anticipate which passages a question requires and discards document-level context that resolves cross-passage references. We introduce evidence-based generation (EBG), requiring models to return an answer with line-level citations, and a joint Ans+Evid metric that scores correctness and grounding simultaneously. We reformulate two corpora into evidence-grounded multi-document QA benchmarks- MultiHop-RAG and QASPER-MP, a multi-paper adaptation of QASPER with realistic short paper cues, and pair them with a controlled synthetic two-hop haystack and an evidence-augmented NoLiMa spanning 10K-1M characters. Across ten proprietary frontier and three open-weight LLMs, EBG isolates two RAG limitations that long-context models avoid: similarity retrieval surfaces any relevant chunk far more reliably than all required chunks for multi-fact queries, and chunking destroys document meta-information needed to resolve identity-bearing queries. EBG also exposes grounding failures invisible to answer-only evaluation, including incomplete citations in two-needle settings and a widening gap between Ans and Ans+Evid when context contradicts parametric knowledge. Data and code are available at https://github.com/debobanerjee/LC-EBG.

papers.title: Where are the higher excited $B$ and $B_s$ mesons with coupled-channel effects?
papers.abstract: Inspired by the newly observed $B_{s0}^*(5700)^0$, whose mass agrees well with our previous unquenched prediction for $B_s(1^3P_0)$ [Phys.~Rev.~D \textbf{109}, 116006 (2024)], we study the mass spectra and OZI-allowed two-body strong decays of the higher $3S$-, $2P$-, $2D$-, and $1F$-wave $B$ and $B_s$ mesons in the same unquenched quark model. Our results show that coupled-channel effects significantly lower the masses and modify the relative level spacings. The scalar state $B(2^3P_0)$ is strongly affected: its mass is lowered well below the quenched quark model predictions, and it mainly decays into $Bπ$. Furthermore, the mass ordering of the vector states $B(2^3D_1)$ and $B(3^3S_1)$ is reversed, and the lighter $B(2^3D_1)$ state mainly decays into $B_1(5721)π$. To test these results, the $B(2^3P_0)$ and $B(2^3D_1)$ states are worth searching for in the $Bπ$ and $B_1(5721)π$ channels, respectively. In addition, some higher excitations are predicted to be relatively narrow and can be searched for in the $B^{(*)}π$, $B^{(*)}K$, $B_1(5721)π/K$, and $B_2^*(5747)π/K$ channels. These predictions provide useful references for future experimental searches and help clarify the role of coupled-channel effects in the heavy-light meson spectrum.

papers.title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Skill-augmented agentic RL has emerged as an effective approach to improving LLM agents on long-horizon tasks. Despite this progress, individual skills may follow distinct trajectories as the policy evolves, with some becoming redundant after the model internalizes their capabilities, others remaining valuable as external scaffolding, and still others turning harmful. However, existing skill library systems fail to identify each skill's true contribution due to free-riding among co-retrieved skills, difficulty confounding across tasks, and the absence of skill-specific counterfactual evidence, which prevents reliable skill lifecycle management. We propose TrackRL, an agentic RL framework where skill tracking drives skill library full lifecycle management. Specifically, within each GRPO group, we turn grouped sampling into online randomized controlled experiments. Independent random injection and within-group contrasts on the same task isolate each skill's true contribution, and reliability-weighted aggregation accumulates evidence across groups. As evidence accumulates, we continuously track skill utility, which measures the skill's causal contribution as external scaffolding, and model mastery, which reflects how far the corresponding capability has been internalized. Along this line, we formulate skill lifecycle management as an evidence-gated state-transition process that governs each skill from generation and admission through protected incubation to retention, retirement, or removal, while a soft capacity bound controls library growth. Experiments show that TrackRL outperforms recent skill-augmented RL baselines in both library-assisted and skill-free evaluation, with further analyses revealing how skill value shifts during policy learning and how evidence-driven state transitions shape skill library evolution. Our code is available at https://github.com/xizhu1022/TrackRL.

papers.title: MemBubble: Benchmarking How Agent Memory Shapes LLM Response Diversity
papers.abstract: Memory serves as the core component of LLM-based agents, enabling personalized responses via extracting and using user preferences from past interactions. However, its use may reduce response diversity, thereby narrowing the range of information available to users. Existing evaluations rely largely on synthetic interactions and cover few memory systems, leaving the effects of memory on response diversity insufficiently evaluated in real-world scenarios. We introduce MemBubble, a benchmark of 1000 instances built on preferences extracted from real user-assistant conversations. To measure the extent to which memory concentrates response distributions, we construct test queries in scenarios distinct from user preferences while preserving topical relevance through shared preference categories. Across multiple LLMs and memory mechanisms, entropy decreases by 34.7% on average compared with directly providing the full interaction history, highlighting the important role of memory processing in diversity loss. We also explore simple user-side interventions and changes in information availability but find that these do not effectively close the diversity gap. Our findings highlight the need to consider preserving diversity and user access to information alongside improvements in personalization when designing and using agent memory systems.

papers.title: Decision-Target Reversal under Informative Label Missingness
papers.abstract: Informative label missingness can improve classification efficiency because the pattern of label availability may itself contain information about the discriminant structure. We show that this advantage need not persist across deployment objectives: with the data-generating model and statistical experiments held fixed, informative partial classification can be favourable under one loss and unfavourable under another. We call this phenomenon decision-target reversal. For binary Gaussian discrimination, we derive a local cost-sensitive excess-risk expansion and, in one dimension, obtain explicit critical cost ratios at which the first-order risk ordering reverses. We show that the required covariance geometry arises under finite uncertainty-dependent missingness mechanisms with a fixed marginal missing-label proportion. We then extend the analysis to multiclass finite-action problems through loss-specific active-boundary curvature, yielding a general decision-target frontier. Monte Carlo experiments illustrate the predicted reversals, and a descriptive gastrointestinal-lesion application with agreement-defined label availability illustrates sensitivity to deployment costs. The results show that favourable informative missingness is a property of the statistical experiment relative to the deployment decision, rather than of the experiment alone.

papers.title: Vector Copula-Based Markov Models
papers.abstract: We propose the vector copula-based Markov model (VCBMM) for describing multivariate time series with nonlinear serial dependence. To extend univariate copula-based Markov models to multivariate time series, we develop a hierarchical construction based on scalar aggregate variables and consider the vector Sklar theorem to obtain the joint density of the VCBMM. We further assume the Clayton copula for serial dependence and the multivariate Gaussian distribution for the marginals. The corresponding likelihood function and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) with the inference functions for margins (IFM) method are provided. The performance of the proposed model is illustrated through simulation studies. In real data analysis, we apply the model to bivariate daily log returns of stocks from the 2008 global financial crisis (2008 GFC) and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic (2020 COVID-19).

papers.title: Structure over Reasoning: Unified Zero-Shot Navigation with a Small Vision-Language Model
papers.abstract: Vision-language navigation is moving into photorealistic, physically simulated scenes, where the leading zero-shot agents put a vision-language model in the control loop to choose every move and stop. Robots favour small models, whose abilities are uneven: Qwen3-VL-4B can judge whether a single view looks like the goal, but its route reasoning is at chance, its distance estimates nearly constant, its stop votes unreliable. Our agent therefore asks it two perceptual questions per step, which direction looks like the goal and whether the view justifies stopping, plus one gated frontier query on route-bearing instructions, and treats the answers as evidence, not actions: a route-blind semantic field over a bird's-eye map accumulates the directional scores through a tempered update, a skeleton graph supplies frontiers and geodesic distances, and a two-stage terminator turns stop votes into termini through a trail-consistency gate and a budget-forced return. With every baseline re-run in one installation at one budget, the agent exceeds all four zero-shot baselines of the VLNVerse subset in mean success on both granularities, though the paired interval against the strongest coarse-grained baseline includes zero. Termination is the dominant lever in ablation, thirteen attempts to give the model more of the navigation establish no reliable gain, and the agent runs on a Unitree Go2 quadruped with off-board inference. Code, per-episode logs and a robot video will be released at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/structure-over-reasoning-PAGE.

papers.title: Data.Readme: Documenting Table Relationships for Diverse Data Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can perform diverse data tasks when given a small set of relevant tables. However, for complex tasks requiring multiple tables over large data lakes, identifying relevant tables for the task becomes a prerequisite, but remains challenging. This is because there are often many tables in a data lake with similar table and schema names, and limited additional semantic context, thereby forcing agents to spend substantial time exploring tables at online query time, greatly affecting models' ability to perform tasks accurately, while increasing cost/latency substantially. We present Data.Readme, a novel table documentation approach that uses lightweight offline processing to infer and index rich \emph{table-to-table relationships}, including confusable, joinable, and union-able tables. We further develop a suite of agentic tools for LLMs to work with the index, to help agents retrieve relevant tables and perform tasks much more efficiently and effectively. Finally, we study how to optimize our index construction with a budget constraint. On data lakes containing up to 12K tables, Data.Readme improves task accuracy by as much as 40 percentage points across a range of data discovery, data analysis, and data science tasks, outperforming diverse baselines, including powerful coding agents with unlimited time and monetary budgets. We also show that equipping existing methods (such as coding agents) with Data.Readme can not only lead to consistent quality gains, but also significantly reduce their latency by up to 6x, demonstrating the potential of Data.Readme.

papers.title: Optical constraints on rotating logarithmic- and exponential-entropy wormholes from strong-field lensing
papers.abstract: The longstanding issue of whether horizonless compact objects can mimic black holes at horizon scales is addressed, a problem that persists because the shadow diameter alone is degenerate across a wide class of geometries. For slowly rotating traversable wormholes, we precisely formulate the optical appearance as a set of observables derived from equatorial null geodesics, yielding necessary and sufficient conditions for a multi-parameter fingerprint. Using a new lapse function that interpolates between exponential and rational redshift profiles, we obtain the photon-sphere condition, the strong-deflection lensing coefficients, and the Lyapunov exponent in closed form. The equations yield two families of wormhole solutions dependent on logarithmic and exponential entropy parameters. We compare the resulting quantum-modified spacetimes with Kerr and four regular black holes. The shadow diameter is shown to be tunable to within $5\%$ to $11\%$ of Kerr for all models considered, so that $|R_{\rm sh}^{\rm WH}/R_{\rm sh}^{\rm Kerr}-1| \lesssim 0.11$ and the shadow alone cannot separate the models. The degeneracy is lifted when the rotational asymmetry, lensing coefficients, Lyapunov exponent, and orbital frequency are combined: for the $5$-component fingerprint $\mathbf{F}=(\Arot,\abar,\bbar, \Lya,\Oph)$, the fractional deviation $Δ_i=(F_i^{\rm WH}-F_i^{\rm Kerr})/ F_i^{\rm Kerr}$ satisfies $|Δ_i|\gtrsim 0.05$ for every component, with the largest departures in the second lensing coefficient and the Lyapunov exponent. The combined discrimination signal reaches a signal-to-noise ratio of about $3.8$ to $3.9$ against Kerr and about $3.7$ against the Kazakov--Solodukhin benchmark, which is sufficient to break the shadow-diameter degeneracy at the $10\%$ measurement level.

papers.title: Many Repairs, One Direction: Steering Code Models Toward Safer Cryptographic API Use
papers.abstract: Cryptographic API misuse in large language model-generated code can compromise software security. While many existing approaches improve code security by modifying model parameters or inputs, how representation changes associated with different cryptographic API repairs can support a shared intervention for safer code generation remains underexplored. To investigate this, we construct 48,000 matched program pairs across four programming languages and ten cryptographic API misuse categories. Each pair changes a specified API decision while preserving the programming task. Subtracting the misuse program's internal representation from its secure counterpart's gives a repair vector. Across five models, comparisons of mean repair vectors reveal stronger organization by misuse category than by language. These category-specific patterns also support a shared intervention. We introduce CrypSteer, which extracts a shared direction by normalizing repair differences and selecting a principal component aligned with repairs across misuse categories. With model weights fixed, adding one shared direction per model to its internal activations during generation improves aggregate target security rates by 5.28--15.00 percentage points over unsteered generation across languages and misuse categories. These findings connect the shared structure of cryptographic repair representations to a reusable intervention for safer code generation.

papers.title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis
papers.abstract: Advancing physics reasoning in large language models requires scalable training data that connect physical laws, concrete problem scenarios, and verifiable numerical answers. Expert-designed problems offer top-down control over physical laws, conditions, and scenarios, but require costly human effort. LLM-based synthesis from texts scales efficiently, but model-generated answers and assessments leave supervision vulnerable to hallucinations. We introduce TIRE, a framework for Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution that brings knowledge-driven problem construction to large-scale data generation.
