papers.abstract: Answering natural language questions over knowledge graph data is challenging due to the vast number of facts, which can be difficult to process and navigate. One potential solution for this issue is to use mined subgraphs related to the query, although this process still requires extracting these subgraphs. This research presents a solution for extracting subgraphs related to entity candidates from a question-and-answer set, which can be obtained by inferring a large language model by calculating the shortest paths between entities. The proposed approaches detail various features that can be extracted from the subgraphs and reranking models to select the most probable answers from a list of candidates. Experiments were conducted on Wikidata to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. This involved enumerating all the main feature types that can be extracted from mined subgraphs and a detailed analysis of the proposed features and reranking method combinations. In addition, a public web application that provides a useful web tool for studying the graph space between question and answer entities has been developed to work with subgraphs. This includes visualization of the extracted subgraph and automatic generation of natural language text to describe it.

papers.title: Electric Hidden Unconventional Collinear Magnetism in 2D \(\mathcal{PT}\)-Symmetric Antiferromagnets
papers.abstract: Electric hidden unconventional collinear magnetism, in which a perpendicular electric field (\(\mathcal{E}_z\)) lifts the \(\mathcal{PT}\)-enforced degeneracy and selectively releases the hidden crystallographic constraints in conventional 2D antiferromagnets to drive emergent magnetic phases, has remained largely unexplored. Here we establish a complete symmetry classification of all 88 collinear spin layer groups (cSLGs) compatible with conventional \(\mathcal{PT}\)-symmetric antiferromagnets, and show that the \(\mathcal{E}_z\) drives the system into three distinct classes of unconventional collinear magnetism: type-IV magnetism (Class-I, 23 cSLGs), altermagnetism (Class-II, 34 cSLGs), and fully compensated ferrimagnetism (Class-III, 31 cSLGs). We illustrate these categories using the most common and feasibly exfoliable 2D candidate materials. These include Sr$_2$CaCr$_2$P$_2$O$_9$ and Sr$_2$CaCr$_2$As$_2$O$_9$ (Class-I), BaMnGe and MnPS$_3$ (Class-II), and Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$ and bilayer MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ (Class-III). We further demonstrate that the \(\mathcal{E}_z\) generates distinctly different spin-splitting fingerprints across the three classes, yielding distinct spin-dependent responses: the electric Hall effect in Class-I, spin-polarized transport in Class-II, and the electric reversible magneto-optical Kerr effect in Class-III. Our work not only closes a complete internal cycle from conventional to unconventional collinear magnetism in 2D antiferromagnets, but also establishes a viable all-electrical compensated magnetism platform and control scheme for future spintronic applications.

papers.title: The chair challenge: can mechanics really tell men from women? A centre-of-mass analysis of a viral party trick
papers.abstract: In the "chair challenge" a person stands several foot lengths from a wall, bends forward until the head touches the wall, lifts a chair and tries to stand up. Online videos suggest that women can do this and men cannot, supposedly because women have a lower centre of mass or men have larger feet. We model the body as a planar chain of rigid segments with standard biomechanical parameters and search all postures allowed by the rules for the one that places the combined centre of mass of body and chair furthest back. As a rule of thumb, the largest toe-wall distance is roughly the trunk-plus-head length minus the distance from hip to centre of mass. For a slow, static rise this limit is 2.36 foot lengths for the male and 2.49 foot lengths for the female reference model, just short of the customary 2.5 foot lengths. The limit is set mainly by trunk-plus-head length relative to foot length, not by the height of the centre of mass; in centimetres the male model actually has more room. With the body proportions of 6068 participants in the 2012 US Army anthropometric survey, the sex difference shrinks from 0.13 to 0.03-0.05 foot lengths, half to one European shoe size. Individually, only 13% of men and 22% of women would pass statically, and predicting sex from the outcome is right in 54-68% of cases (for equal numbers of men and women), against 50% for a coin and 83% for a tape measure. Shoes, age and momentum matter more than the residual sex difference. The problem suits first-year undergraduate mechanics, combining static equilibrium of an articulated body, scaling and units, an inverted-pendulum estimate and a simple classification problem. The chair challenge is a fine demonstration of static equilibrium and a lousy sex predictor.

papers.title: Strategy recovery for Mean-Payoff Games is as hard as solving them from scratch
papers.abstract: Mean-Payoff Games (MPGs) form an interesting family of deterministic, infinite-duration, zero-sum, turn-based games played by two players on a finite weighted directed graph. The goal of the players is to minimize, respectively maximize, the $\textit{limiting average}$ of the costs of the edges on an infinite path constructed by the two players. The complexity of solving MPGs is a long-standing open question. The decision problem associated with these games is known to be in $\text{NP}\cap \text{co-NP}$, and even $\text{UP}\cap \text{co-UP}$, yet the problem is not known to be in $\text{P}$. This is one of the simplest combinatorial problems with such a status. A full solution of an MPG gives the $\textit{value}$ of each vertex of the game, along with a pair of $\textit{optimal strategies}$ for the two players. (Each player has a succinct $\textit{positional}$ optimal strategy.) The problem of finding optimal strategies for the players given the values of all vertices is known as the $\textit{strategy recovery}$ problem. We describe a simple reduction from the problem of solving MPGs to the strategy recovery problem for MPGs. This shows that the strategy recovery problem for MPGs is essentially as hard as solving MPGs from scratch, i.e., without knowing the values. The reduction uses simple $\textit{game transformations}$ and simple $\textit{self-reducibility}$ and $\textit{peeling}$ arguments. This answers a question of Andersson and Miltersen. Mamino obtained a similar result for $\textit{stochastic}$ games with a limiting average objective, but his technique does not extend to deterministic games such as MPGs. We go one step further and show that finding an optimal strategy for one of the players of an MPG remains hard even if an optimal strategy of the second player, and hence all the values, are known.

papers.title: SCOPE: Source Credibility and Outlet Profiling Engine
papers.abstract: We present SCOPE, a multi-agent system for profiling news media outlets with respect to bias, factuality, and credibility. Given an outlet URL, SCOPE coordinates specialized agents for article acquisition, content analysis, external evidence search, scoring, and report generation. The system follows an MBFC-style methodology while making intermediate evidence and agent outputs inspectable through a structured demonstration interface. On a benchmark of 200 media outlets, SCOPE outperforms LLM-only, article-only, search-only, and media-background-check baselines on most metrics, achieving the lowest bias and factuality MAE, perfect failed-fact-check detection, and the lowest factual error rate. These results suggest that decomposed, evidence-grounded agent workflows can support more transparent and reliable media profiling. Our code is available at https://github.com/mbaisbay/SCOPE, and a live demonstration at https://scope-demo.streamlit.app/.

papers.title: Quantum Veto Parton Shower Algorithm in the Conformal Window
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum veto parton shower algorithm for a confining dark sector with gauge symmetry $\mathrm{SU}(3)_D \times \mathrm{U}(1)_D$ operating in the conformal window ($N_C = 3$, $N_F = 12$). The non-Abelian gauge coupling exhibits two-loop running toward an infrared fixed point before decoupling at a finite dark-quark mass threshold, while the dark quarks carry non-degenerate $\mathrm{U}(1)_D$ charges with unitary flavor mixing between the interaction and mass bases. Shower evolution proceeds coherently in the interaction basis, with states prepared and measured in the mass basis. Compared with the classical Markovian shower, the flavor-coherent quantum simulation produces a significantly enhanced zero-emission rate, and a characteristic U-shaped mass-eigenstate spectrum. Furthermore, energy-energy correlators exhibit approximate linearity in the double-logarithmic coordinates over an intermediate angular range, suggesting power-law scaling in that region. This framework demonstrates the capability of quantum algorithms to capture multi-flavor quantum interference in strongly interacting hidden sectors.

papers.title: Unconventional spin momentum locking and topological domains in twisted slabs of topological insulator Bi$_2$Te$_3$
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional topological insulator Bi$_2$Te$_3$ hosts topological Dirac states on its two-dimensional surfaces. These Dirac states show spin-momentum locking, which usually implies a tangential Rashba-like spin texture. One can alter the properties of the Dirac states by dividing a slab of such a material into two thinner halves, modifying the interface by twisting, shifting, and changing the interlayer distance. Using first-principles calculations, we investigate such modified slabs of Bi$_2$Te$_3$. The twisting degree of freedom deserves special attention. To this end, we follow two approaches. On the one hand, we probe different stacking configurations in order to extract parameters relevant for small twist angle Moiré structures. We find non-trivial topology only for some stackings, leading to topological domains on the Moiré scale. On the other hand, we calculate the properties of commensurate twisted supercells. The latter reveals not only flat bands, which are tunable by external pressure, but also radial spin textures with unconventional spin-momentum locking.

papers.title: Sampling and Curvature in First-Exit Comparisons for Momentum SGD
papers.abstract: First-exit prediction for momentum SGD depends on sampling information that pointwise gradient laws omit. Strongly convex finite pools with identical pointwise laws and matched iid momentum dynamics can have different reshuffled exits; even analytic pools with uniformly close pointwise laws can have separated exit probabilities. For persistent sampling in one dimension, we establish an explicit $O(h)$ mean-exit comparison with a finite-rate switching process under nonvanishing component velocities and step-size conditions; iid sampling instead averages to an ODE. Retaining realized minibatches and sampled curvature yields finite-window exit brackets beyond this regime. In 32 trained ridge-logistic runs, 29 meet prespecified targets with rounding-certified brackets; an enclosure control explains most of the width advantage. Exact-real certificates establish finite means at the original tested radii for three ResNet-18 checkpoints and give local finite-mean conditions for tanh and ViT networks; their upper bounds remain loose, and original-radius ViT mean guarantees remain unresolved despite 128 fresh continuation paths. A two-network replication gives 32/32 successful seeds in each of four finite-path persistence comparisons. Independent equal-length controls retain slower exits after refresh resets than without resets, but the refresh-versus-random ordering reverses with update length at both networks. These interventions do not causally decompose raw momentum SGD. Neural step-size scaling does not validate the switching limit.

papers.title: Acharya 2.0: An AI Tutor for Self-Learning Subjects in Hindi
papers.abstract: Text processing is crucial for low-resource languages as it enables the development of tools and technologies that bridge the digital divide and provide equitable access to information and services. By empowering low-resource languages with robust text processing, we can preserve linguistic diversity, enhance education, improve communi- cation, and foster inclusivity in a rapidly digitizing world. Due to the lack of sufficient annotated datasets and lin- guistic resources, it is challenging to develop accurate and reliable language technologies for these low-resource languages. Large Language Models (LLMs) have attracted sig- nificant attention with their performance and the value they produce. However, with the ever-evolving language, adapting LLMs for a specific task is time-consuming and resource-intensive. Thus, Retrieval-Augmented Genera- tion (RAG) has overcome this limitation by augmenting LLMs with external knowledge, thereby improving their efficiency and extensive task-specific adaptation. Most applications of the RAG technique have been limited to English and has seen limited application in In- dic languages. This paper introduces the RAG-powered AI-Tutor application, Acharya 2.0, designed to produce academic assistance to Hindi-speaking students. The client-server-based web application integrates many fea- tures to support students in accessing and interacting with educational content.

papers.title: Shallow Probes Are Sufficient for Near-Oracle Personalization Depth Allocation in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Rather than proposing a new federated optimizer, we study whether a small client-specific measurement budget can support cost-aware personalization-depth decisions under a utility that trades Macro-F1 against deployment cost. Exhaustive evaluation of six depths defines an offline oracle that is not deployable. We audit the Probe Sufficiency Hypothesis: three shallow probes (P0--P2) may contain most decision-relevant information for approaching that oracle. FedPBA is a secondary learned instantiation for deep-action extrapolation. On CIFAR-10/100 and patient-disjoint PTB-XL (45 sessions; 900 clients; 2700 evaluations; GroupKFold), training-free greedy probing achieves regret 0.0071 and 98.3 percent oracle recovery, beating metadata-only policies and FedPBA (0.0110 / 97.3 percent). Aggregate shallow-best versus oracle correlation is 0.9818 but falls to 0.578 on deep-oracle rows; PTB-XL deep-oracle cases remain a high-regret boundary without a validated escalation gate.

papers.title: Electronic structure, magnetic order and anisotropic magnetoresistance in $\mathbf{Eu_{1-x}Gd_xCd_2P_2}$ (0 $\le$ x $\le$1)
papers.abstract: Recently, $\text{EuCd}_2\text{P}_2$ has attracted increased attention for its colossal magnetoresistive (CMR) property, the mechanism of which seems to deviate from that of known canonical CMR compounds such as manganites. Many studies underscore the role of low density of hole carriers caused by Eu vacancies, particularly in stabilizing ferromagnetic (FM) order and modifying electrical transport and magnetoresistive responses in this compound. A magnetic polaron based mechanism rather than double exchange based mechanism is being proposed to explain the CMR effect for this compound. In this work, we explore the effect of elctron doping on the magnetic transition and CMR behaviour via Gd substitution at Eu sites with varying concentration (x) in Eu$_{1-x}$Gd$_{x}$Cd$_2$P$_2$. Our Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Monte Carlo-based calculations reveal an oscillating ground state magnetic order as a function of electron carrier density. The ground state is found to be A-AFM metal for x=0.056, 0.125 and 0.5 while it becomes ferromagnetic metal at x= 0.33, 0.67 and 1. Most importantly, we predict colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance in this compound for x=0.125 and 0.5. The underlying mechanism of anisotropic CMR in this compound looks similar to double exchange like due to the presence of a strong intra-site 4\textit{f}-5\textit{d} ferromagnetic exchange interaction and an itinerant electron in the hybridized conduction states. The oscillating ground state magnetic order and the enhancement of transition temperature (as high as 150K for x=0.67) as a function of electron carrier density offers a new avenue to tune the magnetotransport property in this compound and offers an excellent platform for designing future spintronics devices.

papers.title: Image Restoration with Impulse Noise Based on Minimax Concave Penalty: Grayscale and Color Images
papers.abstract: In today's world-where social networks play a significant role-images serve as one of the most important tools for transferring concepts. Image degradation caused by noise or blurring hinders the effective transmission of the information we expect to derive from an image. Consequently, developing image restoration methods capable of revealing crucial information is of great importance. In this work, a model for impulse noise image restoring is proposed by using a Minimax Concave Penalty. The proposed model is applicable to both color and grayscale images. Then, a numerical algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers is introduced, and the convergence of the method is analyzed both theoretically and numerically. In the final step, the proposed method is evaluated through simulations on several examples, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness.

papers.title: Exact probability laws of random inner products: Dirichlet splines, overlaps, uncertainty, and Bargmann invariants
papers.abstract: Inner products of random matrices and random quantum states---such as orbital inner products, expectation values, overlaps, and cyclic Bargmann invariants---are shown to follow from two underlying mechanisms: the diagonal of an induced random state is Dirichlet distributed, and the expectation value of a random pure state in a rank-one or two-by-two operator is a numerical shadow on an elliptical disk. For states induced by an environment of dimension $K$, the expectation value of any observable is a Curry--Schoenberg spline with each eigenvalue repeated $K$ times, and the vector of moments has an explicit density on a simplex; for a qutrit, the variance law is obtained in finite form. The overlap of two random qubit states attains its mode at its mean for every rotation-invariant ensemble, but for Hilbert--Schmidt qutrits the density at the mean has a strictly negative derivative, so mode and mean separate; for large environments, the centred overlap converges to a variance-gamma law rather than a Gaussian. For two noncommuting qubit observables, the joint law of the two standard deviations is derived for all $K$, and the probability of coming within a small distance of the optimal sum of variances scales as a power of that distance, with a different exponent when the Bloch axes are orthogonal. For three Haar-random qubit states, the exact density of the Bargmann invariant is given in terms of a complete elliptic integral, together with its local behaviour and elementary marginals. In every dimension, the probability that its real part is negative---certifying basis-independent coherence---is computed, along with all mixed moments. For cycles of arbitrary length, the invariant is shown to be driven by an exact three-parameter Markov chain, and the logarithm of its modulus obeys a law of large numbers and a central limit theorem.

papers.title: Gerchberg-Saxton Optimized Silicon Metasurface for Sinusoidal Structured-Light Three-Dimensional Imaging
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) optical imaging based on structured illumination has attracted considerable attention in applications including machine vision, robotics, and computational sensing. However, conventional structured-light systems generally rely on bulky projection components, such as digital micromirror devices and diffractive optical elements, which limit system miniaturization and integration. Here, we demonstrate a compact structured-light 3D imaging platform enabled by a silicon dielectric metasurface operating at a near-infrared wavelength of 940 nm. The desired sinusoidal fringe illumination is encoded into the metasurface through a Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) phase optimization algorithm, which converts the target far-field distribution into a nanoscale phase profile and subsequently into silicon nanopillar geometries. The fabricated metasurface generates high-quality sinusoidal structured illumination, which is integrated with a four-step phase-shifting reconstruction method to recover 3D object profiles. The proposed approach provides a compact and scalable solution for miniaturized structured-light projection and optical 3D sensing.

papers.title: Taming Cyclic Dependencies in Stabilization-Based String Constraint Solving
papers.abstract: Word equations with cyclic variable dependencies pose a challenge to SMT string solvers. In stabilization-based procedures, such dependencies can trigger repeated refinement of regular-language assignments without reaching stability. We present Z3-Noodler-C, an extension of Z3-Noodler, combining equality-aware stabilization with dedicated loop reasoning. We introduce equality predicates to retain relevant equations as single stability obligations, and extend stabilization with equality-aware substitution and adapted concatenation-eliminating refinement to expose cyclic dependencies as overlapping variable bindings. Dedicated loop reasoning rules then exploit the periodic structure of these bindings, avoiding certain infinite derivations. We evaluate Z3-Noodler-C against Z3-Noodler, cvc5 and OSTRICH2. On 64 systematically generated, syntactically simple instances involving cyclic dependencies and regular constraints, our solver solves all instances, compared with only 20 solved for the best baseline. On equation-oriented instances from SMT-LIB'25, Z3-Noodler-C achieves the highest coverage, solving 20 more instances than Z3-Noodler while maintaining competitive aggregate CPU time.

papers.title: On the Nature of the BeWD System Nova FQ Circinus
papers.abstract: The classical nova FQ Cir (Schaefer et al. 2026) has recently been shown to have a Be star donor, and has been identified as a High Mass Cataclysmic Variable (HMCV), with an orbital period of $\sim 2.04d$ (twice the 1.02d periodogram peak). Using the extensive OGLE optical archive, together with existing observations from ASAS-SN we instead find significant modulation between $\sim 50-60$~days and propose that the orbital period is likely closer to $\sim 62d$. We interpret the low amplitude 1.02 d modulation as a non-radial pulsation of the Be star. We also reassess the HMCV classification based on properties of known Be star-white dwarf systems.

papers.title: A nontopological triangulated category which is $θ$-dg enhanced
papers.abstract: For every nonzero commutative ring $R$ and infinite cardinal $θ$, we construct a nontopological triangulated category over $R$, whose thick subcategories generated by $<θ$ objects admit $R$-linear dg enhancements, while the scalar action of $R$ is faithful.

papers.title: ChronoChart: Setup-Agnostic Channel Charting for Label-Free Indoor Localization
papers.abstract: Accurate radio-based indoor localization remains challenging in multipath-rich and dynamic indoor environments. Supervised fingerprinting methods achieve high positioning accuracy by learning mappings from radio channel measurements to physical locations, but require costly position labels and frequent recalibration. Channel Charting (CC) addresses this limitation by learning low-dimensional representations of Channel State Information (CSI) without position labels, yielding channel charts in which nearby points correspond to nearby physical locations. However, prominent CC methods rely on setup-specific dissimilarity metrics, such as ADP-, CIRA-, or PDR-based distances, and on precomputed $O(n^2)$ distance matrices, limiting scalability and transferability across radio systems. We propose ChronoChart, a timestamp-supervised CC framework that requires only CSI and timestamps without prior knowledge for training. Our method jointly optimizes complementary objectives: a triplet loss using temporally derived positive and negative samples to establish coarse global structure, a temporal-proximity loss that promotes smooth trajectories in the chart, and a joint-embedding loss that enforces consistency between representations of different augmentations. Evaluated on real-world 5G, MIMO, and passive UWB data, our method matches or exceeds prior CC baselines that depend on tailored distance metrics, and remains scalable and applicable across heterogeneous radio systems.

papers.title: IMF-aware N-body forward modelling of membership selection functions for young open clusters
papers.abstract: We present an IMF-aware N-body forward-modelling framework, in which the stellar initial mass function (IMF) is an explicit input, to quantify the membership selection functions of open clusters, namely completeness and contamination as functions of magnitude. Accurate derivation of the IMF requires correcting for these selection effects, which otherwise distort the inferred present-day mass function. Our framework simulates clusters with IMF slopes $α_2 = -2.7, -2.3, -1.9$, converts them into synthetic Gaia observations, adds mock field populations, and recovers members with HDBSCAN to mimic observational membership selection. Applying this framework to 35 young open clusters (ages $\lesssim100$ Myr, distances $\lesssim600$ pc), we find declining completeness towards the faint limit; older, more expanded, and more diffuse models have lower completeness and higher contamination. For a given cluster, models with flatter IMFs yield modestly but systematically lower global completeness and higher contamination, despite initial cluster masses calibrated to the same observed member count. These models undergo more stellar evolution mass loss and expand more, resulting in lower projected stellar densities; their lower completeness is consistent with more diffuse clusters being harder to separate from field stars. Corrections derived from a mismatched IMF largely recover the total star counts but leave a larger distortion in the shape of the present-day luminosity function than those derived with the correct IMF. Because membership recovery is tied to a cluster's structural evolution and the specific membership algorithm used, our findings emphasize that selection functions should be inferred jointly with the IMF rather than assumed in advance.

papers.title: RAIL-5G: A Challenging Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for AI-Based 5G Indoor Localization
papers.abstract: Reliable radio-based indoor localization is essential for industrial automation, yet existing methods are often evaluated in environments that do not fully reflect the severe multipath and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions encountered in real deployments. This limits our understanding of how AI, i.e., modern geometric, unsupervised, and semi-supervised localization methods generalize to industrial 5G settings. We present RAIL-5G, a public real-world 5G NR channel impulse response (CIR) benchmark recorded in an operational railway maintenance facility. RAIL-5G covers an 811m$^2$ indoor area with eight distributed radio units, robot-mounted user equipment (UE) trajectories, high-accuracy iGPS reference positions, and severe metal-induced multipath caused by train compartments and maintenance infrastructure. We benchmark geometric time-difference of arrival (TDoA), supervised fingerprinting, unsupervised channel charting, and self-supervised wireless pretraining methods. Our results highlight the difficulty of RAIL-5G: on the full dataset, TDoA reaches 7.02m mean average error (MAE), the best unsupervised method reaches 2.46m, and supervised fingerprinting achieves 0.52m. Self-supervised pretraining reduces the labeling effort by up to one order of magnitude, but the remaining gap to supervised learning shows that robust AI-based localization under severe multipath remains an open challenge. The dataset and code are available at https://iis.fraunhofer.de/rail-5g.

papers.title: ViCoR: Estimating Visual Necessity via Counterfactual Residuals for Multimodal Medical Data Selection
papers.abstract: Medical vision-language models often exhibit hidden stratification, where high overall performance masks failures on subtle visual findings and overlapping clinical conditions. We trace this failure mode to modality imbalance during fine-tuning, where strong linguistic priors can suppress visually grounded learning and induce plausible but weakly grounded rationales. Existing data selection methods usually score image-text pairs as holistic units, without separating visually necessary samples from shortcut-solvable ones. To address this problem, we propose ViCoR, a counterfactual-residual-based data selection method for Med-VLM fine-tuning. ViCoR estimates visual necessity through image-dependent optimization residuals, calibrates the resulting scores with medical supervision compatibility, and constructs a diversity-aware fine-tuning subset. Across two backbones, four external generalization benchmarks, and one multi-disease robustness benchmark, ViCoR-selected 20\% subsets achieve the strongest average performance compared with full-data fine-tuning and selection baselines. Gradient-level analysis and perturbation audits further show that ViCoR enriches image-dependent training signals and strengthens image-level and evidence-region dependence. The code will be available at https://github.com/htgan-ai/ViCoR.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Quantum Forensics for QKD: Machine Learning Attack Detection and Signature Extraction
papers.abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) supports secure key establishment under ideal protocol assumptions, but practical systems remain exposed to implementation-level attacks against optical channels, detectors, and controller behavior. This study presents Quantum Forensic Log (QF-LOG), a simulation-based forensic framework for analyzing aggregated QKD operational logs rather than raw quantum states. QF-LOG uses four observable features: quantum bit error rate (QBER), photon count, latency in milliseconds, and abort flag. The framework classifies normal operation and three simulated attack-related conditions: partial intercept-resend, detector-blind, and fiber-tap. A physics-inspired Generator-A dataset with 5 million balanced records was constructed using explicit mathematical generation models for all four features. A transparent threshold baseline, logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were evaluated on Generator-A. The full-feature learning models achieved macro F1-scores from 0.8211 to 0.8243 and outperformed the transparent two-feature comparator. Feature diagnostics showed that QBER contributed most, followed by latency in milliseconds and photon count, while no single feature reproduced the full feature set performance. Robustness was assessed on a separately generated Generator-B dataset of 5 million records that uses the same governing equations under shifted simulated operating parameters. Without retraining or tuning, their macro F1-scores decreased to values from 0.5645 to 0.5669. These findings show that QF-LOG can support interpretable forensic classification in a controlled synthetic setting, but stable internal evaluation does not establish reliability under changed simulated QKD operating conditions. The framework provides a documented basis for future evaluation across broader simulated settings and hardware-generated QKD logs.

papers.title: Crossing numbers of complete bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: Zarankiewicz's long standing conjecture states that the crossing number $cr(K_{m,n})$ of the complete bipartite graph is \[ Z(m,n):=\bigg\lfloor{\frac{m}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{m-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor. \] Using flag algebras, we show that $cr(K_{n,n}) \geq 0.96936 \cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. We also show that the rectilinear crossing number $\overline{cr}(K_{n,n})$ of $K_{n,n}$ is at least $0.987\cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. Additionally, we prove the following for complete bipartite graphs: if a drawing of $K_{n,n}$ contains no induced subdrawing of $K_{3,4}$ with exactly two crossings whose endpoints intersect in exactly one vertex, then it has at least $Z(n,n)+o(n^4)$ crossings. This is a local restriction inspired by Turán-type problems that gives an asymptotically tight result. A closely related conjecture is Hill's conjecture stating that the crossing number $cr(K_{n})$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is \[ H(n):= \frac14 \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor \] for all $n \geq 3$. By an averaging argument, the asymptotic Zarankiewicz conjecture implies the asymptotic Hill conjecture. We improve the lower bound on $cr(K_{n})$ from $(0.985+o(1)) H(n)$ to $(0.9899+o(1)) H(n)$. Both conjectures were claimed to be true in manuscripts by OpenAI dated Sep 23, 2026 and made public on Oct 6, 2026. This paper represents the state of knowledge before those publications and shows how far we can push the flag algebra method.

papers.title: A relationship between three-dimensional Bessel processes in terms of Pitman's transformation
papers.abstract: For every $x\ge 0$, let $R^{x}=\{ R^{x}_{t}\} _{t\ge 0}$ be a three-dimensional Bessel process started at $x$. Given $x>0$, with the aid of Pitman's theorem, a path transformation $T_{x}$ under which the process $T_{x}(R^{y})$ is distributed as $R^{x}$ for any $y>0$ is constructed. In fact, we prove that, for every $x,y>0$, the two three-dimensional processes \begin{align*} \bigl( R^{x},T_{y}(R^{x}),\mathcal{P}(-R^{x})+x\bigr) && \text{and} && \bigl( T_{x}(R^{y}),R^{y},\mathcal{P}(-R^{y})+y\bigr) \end{align*} are identical in law, where $\mathcal{P}$ is Pitman's transformation. In the course of our exploration, it will be revealed that, for any $x>0$, the process $\mathcal{P}(-R^{x})+x$ has the same law as the standard three-dimensional Bessel process $R^{0}$, which is then applied to derive a disintegration formula for the law of $R^{x}$ in terms of Pitman's transformation. An application of the formula to three-dimensional Bessel bridges is also presented.

papers.title: Linear Structure, Convergence and Resurgence of Hydrodynamic Transseries
papers.abstract: We construct an exact formulation for the solution of Bjorken expanding relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with a constant relaxation time and derive its late time transseries structure. The two fundamental modes of the linear auxiliary equation separate the hydrodynamic contribution from the exponentially suppressed transient mode. We show that this single transient mode generates the entire hierarchy of nonperturbative sectors through nonlinear mode mixing, while its decay explains the loss of initial condition dependence and the emergence of late time hydrodynamic attractor behavior. The hydrodynamic gradient expansion is factorially divergent for generic values of the transport parameter but converges at the discrete values $a=N^2$, where the auxiliary asymptotic expansions terminate. We further determine the exact Stokes constant of the auxiliary linear equation and establish its relation to the logarithmic Borel singularity coefficient. The vanishing of the Stokes constant at these exceptional values establishes a direct connection between auxiliary series termination, hydrodynamic convergence, and Stokes decoupling between the hydrodynamic and the nonhydrodynamic transient sector.

papers.title: Dynamic System Inspired Continuous Large Language Model for AI4Science Tasks
papers.abstract: Scientific foundation models increasingly operate on continuous phenomena, yet still use discrete residual computation. We ask whether pretrained residual transformations can support additional latent computation without expanding the backbone. To test this possibility, we introduce Continuum-LM, which reuses these transformations as dynamical operators in a continuous-depth language model. Its hidden states evolve through an ordinary differential equation evaluated by higher-order numerical integration, with solver order and step size controlling computation. Across eight scientific tasks, Continuum-LM trains stably and improves mean exact-match accuracy by 7.77 and 10.96 percentage points over discrete counterparts at the 0.6B and 1.7B scales, respectively. At 0.6B, it also outperforms an Ouro-style recurrent control under matched parameter and residual-function evaluation budgets. Together, these results support extensible computational depth through parameter reuse, identifying continuous hidden-state evolution as a practical design dimension for scientific language models beyond parameter scaling.

papers.title: A Thousand Faces: A Persuasion Benchmark with Experience-Grounded Persuadees Informed by Psychology and Pragmatics
papers.abstract: People can express the same beliefs and desires yet need different reasons to change their minds. What makes an argument relevant depends on how those views arose: experiences shape what a person finds credible, what matters to them, and what could prompt reconsideration. These personal grounds may also be expressed indirectly, through contextual clues in conversation. Benchmarks that specify beliefs and desires without these connections can reward arguments that match a description while overlooking whether they address the person's reasons. We introduce A Thousand Faces (ATF-Persu), with 1,000 personas across 200 topics and nine domains. Drawing on personality and attitude theories and conversational implicature, we construct five personas per factual context, linking experiences to judgments, expression, and grounds for revision. Evaluations show lower persuasion success than three comparison benchmarks under their respective protocols. Complete backgrounds yield broader use of supplied personal grounds and higher persona faithfulness than simplified specifications; blinded reviewers also rate ATF-Persu above CToMPersu on identifiable personal reasons, their influence on responses, and contextual expression. The dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Slandes/ATF-Persu.

papers.title: Condensation and Non-condensation in the Quasilinear 4-wave Kinetic Equation
papers.abstract: We study finite-time condensation at zero frequency for the isotropic quasilinear 4-wave kinetic equation in three dimensions. With Schrodinger dispersion and a product interaction coefficient with exponent $β\in(0,3/4]$, we construct global measure solutions $(g_t)_{t\geq0}$ for every nonnegative initial measure $g_0$ with finite wave action and energy. We then establish the sharp threshold $β=1/4$ for finite-time condensation of the constructed solutions. For $β\in[1/4,3/4]$, the constructed solutions satisfy $g_t(\{0\})=g_0(\{0\})$ for all $t\geq0$. For $β\in(0,1/4)$, every constructed solution with $(g_0)_{\mathrm{ac}}\neq0$ satisfies $\|g_t-\mathcal{N}_0δ_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq C\mathcal{N}_0(1+\mathcal{N}_0^2t)^{-(1-4β)/40}$ for all $t\geq0$, where $\mathcal{N}_0=g_0([0,\infty))$ and $C=C(β,g_0/\mathcal{N}_0)>0$. In particular, for every $ζ\in(0,1)$, there exists $T_ζ<\infty$ such that $g_t(\{0\})\geq(1-ζ)\mathcal{N}_0$ for all $t\geq T_ζ$.

papers.title: BrandEval: A Two-Track Multi-Agent Benchmark for Risk-Sensitive LLM Crisis Communication
papers.abstract: Evaluating LLMs for crisis communication requires more than judging isolated responses, because public feedback and competitor actions can reshape trust over time. Existing benchmarks remain largely static and single-turn, offering limited evidence about long-horizon risk-sensitive communication. We introduce \textbf{BrandEval}, a two-track benchmark for product-crisis communication, focusing on public brand responses to product-related safety, quality, service, and trust incidents. BrandEval-Static evaluates stakeholder-aware strategic analysis, while BrandEval-Dynamic stress-tests response policies in \textbf{BrandPolis}, a controlled multi-agent sandbox with consumer feedback, competitor responses, and trust-risk trajectories. We also construct \textbf{BrandSRD}, a Chinese crisis-response dataset, and instantiate a reference Strategic Agent using \textbf{Strategic Rationale (SR)}. Across proprietary and open-source models, we find that static strategic quality is informative but incomplete: it aligns with some end-state outcomes but does not reliably predict volatility and delayed recovery; dynamic stress tests further expose tail-risk failures under manipulative or weakly grounded policies. The code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/htgan-ai/BrandEval.

papers.title: One Component Plasmas Frequency Moments from the ISF
papers.abstract: Dynamic structural characteristics of classical one component plasmas (OCP) are an essential tool for understanding of strongly coupled plasmas through experiments and numerical simulations. Here, instead of the dynamic structure factor, we focus our attention on the intermediate scattering function (ISF). Theoretical results are compared to those of obtained by the method of molecular dynamics (MD).

papers.title: VS-Flash: Harnessing Vector Search with Computational Memory-Semantic Flash
papers.abstract: As generative AI continues to evolve, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems are driving rapid growth in vector database capacity requirements. As datasets outgrow host DRAM, vector databases rely on MMap-based serving over SSDs to extend capacity. However, high-fan-out ANN searches generate concurrent irregular accesses that contend for host memory and storage resources, degrading bulk throughput and inflating tail latency under mixed workloads. In this paper, we address these challenges through memory-semantic capacity and workload-aware compute placement. VS-Flash exposes flash as a large-capacity memory-semantic space and dynamically selects the execution engine according to runtime query and workload characteristics. It offloads throughput-oriented large-batch queries to a Computational Memory-Semantic Flash (CMS-Flash) device, while executing latency-sensitive small-batch queries on the host CPU. Both paths access the same resident segments, avoiding a separate host-DRAM replica. Across three billion-scale datasets, VS-Flash improves bulk-search throughput over vanilla Milvus by 36.8X on average, with up to a 57.4X improvement. Under mixed workloads, VS-Flash reduces the p99 latency of latency-sensitive requests by up to 24.8X while sustaining device-side bulk search. These results show that VS-Flash delivers scalable vector search beyond host DRAM capacity while jointly improving bulk throughput and small-request tail latency.

papers.title: Negative partisanship drives anti-frontrunner volatility in election dynamics
papers.abstract: Negative partisanship-where voter mobilization is driven primarily by aversion toward an opposing candidate rather than positive alignment-profoundly reshapes modern electoral dynamics. Here, we formulate a two-dimensional piecewise map to model campaign opinion dynamics, where voter abstention arises endogenously from a latent spectrum of voter activation barriers. We show that cross-candidate rejection sensitivity triggers a non-smooth collapse of abstention, dividing the phase space into an under-mobilized regime and a fully mobilized campaign regime. In symmetric elections with radicalized voter bases, spontaneous symmetry breaking via a pitchfork bifurcation gives rise to asymmetric polling attractors partitioned by mirror-symmetric basins of attraction, where early public perceptions-encoded in initial campaign conditions-act as a deterministic catalyst selecting candidate lead lock-in long before election day. For elevated cross-rejection, the symmetric equilibrium destabilizes via a period-doubling flip bifurcation, driving persistent anti-frontrunner polling swings. Rather than predicting static candidate hegemony, our model reveals that high negative partisanship turns elections into time-sensitive dynamical systems, where final election outcomes reflect discrete sampling snapshots of an oscillating campaign trajectory.

papers.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research
papers.abstract: EEG analysis and decoding underpin brain-computer interfaces, cognitive assessment, and sleep monitoring. Fixed pipelines and reward-driven search do not explicitly determine how signal structure, representations, predictor behavior, and training dynamics contribute to performance or generalization gaps, leaving intervention choice underdetermined. We introduce NeuroAct, an autonomous research agent framework for EEG analysis and decoding. NeuroAct implements dual-loop autonomous research across EEG foundation models, task-specific predictors, and model combinations. In an inner loop, research, development, and review roles use evidence on signal structure, representations, predictor behavior, and training dynamics to test hypotheses, select analyses or interventions, and refine candidates using performance, stability, and cost feedback. An outer loop distills outcomes into conditional, testable recommendations with task and model conditions, then validates and revises them on subsequent tasks.We evaluate four settings: (A) EEG General Analysis, (B) Cross-task Model Optimization, (C) Single-task Open Research, and (D) Collaborative Prediction. In Setting A, NeuroAct's 80.88 macro-average exceeds BrainAgent's 63.13 by 17.75 points. In Setting B, NeuroAct raises EEGPT's mean balanced accuracy (BA) by 7.34 points and HBN Pearson's (r) from 0.6894 to 0.7362; in Setting C, it improves ADFTD BA by 16.33 points; and in Setting D, it raises Workload BA from 79.69% to 85.02%. Experience reuse raises BCIC-IV-2a BA from 34.66% to 50.81% while reducing LLM tokens by 64.02%, indicating recommendations improve cross-task performance. NeuroAct enables evidence-guided EEG research improved by cross-task experience.

papers.title: Calibration-Free Early Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via E-processes
papers.abstract: Reasoning large language models (LLMs) benefit from test-time scaling, motivating adaptive policies that spend tokens when they help and stop early otherwise. Existing rules halt when a confidence or stability signal crosses a threshold, but such thresholds rarely transfer across models and datasets, and validation-calibrated rules lose their guarantee under shifts in test-time horizon or signal dynamics. We reframe adaptive stopping as sequential evidence accumulation along the reasoning trajectory rather than threshold calibration on held-out data. Our framework runs two e-processes on a shared per-chunk signal: a commit stream tracks the signal's position relative to its slow trend, and an abstain stream tracks its signed velocity, making the two anti-correlated by construction. Under signal-level nulls on the per-chunk increments, Ville's inequality yields an anytime-valid signal-level false-alarm bound at user-specified significance levels, with no held-out calibration. Across various model--dataset combinations, the framework matches or exceeds calibration-based stopping on the token--accuracy Pareto front using zero calibration data, and the same significance level transfers unchanged across cells where calibration becomes infeasible.

papers.title: LiftDiff: Guided Discrete Diffusion for Quantum Code Construction
papers.abstract: The realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation relies on Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECC). Of particular interest are codes that combine a high encoding rate with sufficient distance. Existing algebraic constructions, such as lifted product (LP) codes, build a large quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code from a classical base matrix. In this work we introduce LiftDiff, a generative approach to the discovery of QECC. A discrete denoising diffusion model is trained to generate base matrices over the group algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[\mathbb{Z}_\ell]$, which are then expanded into LP codes. The reverse diffusion process is guided by an energy function that evaluates quantum code properties, including girth, degree, sparsity and decoding performance, steering the sampler toward matrices that yield LP codes with favorable parameters. Our method discovers codes with parameters such as $[[169,13,11]]$, $[[143,15,9]]$, and $[[260,24,10]]$, including a $[[247,19,14]]$ code that achieves the highest ${kd^2}/{n}$ among the baselines. Moreover, several discovered codes outperform the Gross code across a broad range of the tested physical error rates under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise.

papers.title: Do LLMs Really Lack Difference Awareness? Uncovering Heuristic Substitution in Group-Differentiating Fairness
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the issue of difference awareness in LLMs, defined as a model's ability to recognize and acknowledge meaningful differences between social groups in fairness decision-making. Previous studies have consistently shown that models perform poorly on such tasks, a finding commonly attributed to a lack of difference awareness. We propose an alternative account, which we term Fairness Heuristic Substitution: difference awareness is not necessarily absent, but the complex demand of simultaneously identifying relevant group differences and determining their implications for fairness decisions may lead models to substitute the simpler, more accessible equal-treatment heuristic, i.e., formal equality. Based on this hypothesis, we introduce TDD, a Two-stage Distinguish-Decide framework that explicitly decomposes fairness reasoning into first distinguishing contextually relevant group differences and then making the corresponding decision, thereby discouraging reliance on formal-equality shortcuts. (i) Across four benchmarks and ten models ranging from billions to trillions of parameters, TDD significantly outperforms one-stage baselines, even one strengthened through simulated test-set leakage. (ii) Combining TDD with neuron-level contrastive probing provides mechanistic evidence consistent with the Fairness Heuristic Substitution hypothesis by revealing two signatures of the formal-equality: a compact, locally coordinated representational structure and a pronounced activation bias under default reasoning. (iii) TDD's stage-wise decomposition uncovers overlooked failure modes in fairness reasoning, including heuristic displacement and misaligned stage dynamics.

papers.title: Lorentz-Invariance Violation with neutrinos from gamma-ray bursts using IceCube High-Energy Starting Events 12-year dataset
papers.abstract: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos provide a unique probe of Lorentz-invariance violation (LIV), as small energy-dependent deviations from the speed of light can produce measurable time delays over cosmological distances. We search for LIV-induced correlations between neutrinos and gamma-ray bursts using the public 12-year IceCube High-Energy Starting Event dataset and a catalog of 746 bursts with measured redshifts. We develop a likelihood analysis accounting for neutrino directional and energy uncertainties, a possible intrinsic time offset between neutrino and gamma-ray emission, and the decay of superluminal neutrinos expected within effective field theory. For linear LIV, the data show a mild preference over the background-only hypothesis, with a $p$-value of $3.1\%$, corresponding to a one-sided Gaussian significance of approximately $1.9σ$. The best fit corresponds to a LIV scale $Λ_{\rm LIV}=5.8\times10^{17}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and is effectively driven by the subluminal component, as superluminal neutrinos are strongly suppressed by LIV-induced decays at the analyzed energies. The preferred LIV scale and the most significant neutrino--gamma-ray burst associations are consistent with previous studies based on different statistical approaches. No evidence for quadratic LIV is found. These results motivate further searches with complementary neutrino datasets, particularly at lower energies, where the superluminal component may become observable.

papers.title: Hidden Cartographer: Hidden State Guided Data Selection for Dual Budgeted Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Given the high cost of expert annotation and limited fine-tuning resources, effective data selection from large unlabeled pools under strict budgets has become a crucial step in adapting LLMs to specialized domains. Existing label-dependent methods risk distorted selection when using pseudo-labels, while traditional active learning methods do not explicitly characterize instruction-tuning dynamics. To address these limitations, we propose Hidden Cartographer (HC), a two-stage framework that uses hidden states to guide annotation and exact training dynamics to select the final training subset. The first stage is Progressive Candidate Expansion, which utilizes the proxy to iteratively select top unlabeled candidates for expert annotation, merging them to recompute training dynamics and update the proxy until the annotation budget is exhausted; the second stage is Exact Cartography Pruning, which ranks these annotated candidates by their exact dynamics scores to isolate a compact subset under the final training budget. Experiments across the medical, legal, and financial domains demonstrate that HC achieves the highest average accuracy among all budgeted baselines, requiring annotation for only 20--30% of the original pool and fine-tuning on just 10--15%.

papers.title: Is there gluonium in the $η^\prime$? The flavour structure of $η$ and $η^\prime$ mixing in radiative $V\to Pγ$ and $P\to Vγ$ decays
papers.abstract: Radiative $V\to Pγ$ and $P\to Vγ$ decays are conventionally described using constituent-quark mass differences and phenomenological wavefunction-overlap factors as sources of flavour-symmetry breaking. We investigate whether the overlap factors can instead be understood as the effect of mixing of the $η$ and $η^\prime$ with an additional pseudoscalar state, described by an $SO(4)$ rotation among four basis states. A global fit to current data yields a significantly better description than the corresponding three-state limit without overlap factors, while preserving the established $η$-$η^\prime$ and vector-meson mixing angles, and shows that the additional state mixes predominantly with the non-strange component. The conventional overlap-factor description is recovered exactly as the special case in which this mixing is purely non-strange. The non-strange pattern disfavours both a flavour-singlet admixture, as expected from mixing with a pseudoscalar glueball, and the gluonium scenario considered in previous analyses. Radiative decays therefore provide no compelling evidence for gluonium in the $η^\prime$, and the overlap factors are better interpreted in terms of a radially excited non-strange state.

papers.title: Non-geometric ideal triangulations with all edge valences at least six
papers.abstract: Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio conjectured that an ideal triangulation in which every edge has valence at least six can be realized by hyperbolic partially truncated tetrahedra on the compact 3-manifold it defines. We show that this is false. Starting from the figure-eight knot complement, we construct an ideal triangulation with $2688$ tetrahedra and edge valences six and eighteen whose manifold is hyperbolic with totally geodesic boundary, but which admits no such realization. The obstruction is a critical point of the covolume energy of Luo and Yang at which three tetrahedra have collapsed: convexity then excludes every geometric competitor, an Euler characteristic count excludes edges of length zero, and the critical point itself is located by a finite certificate in exact integer arithmetic. The obstruction persists in every finite cover, while a complementary theorem shows that no counterexample can have only two edge lengths or only two orbits of edges.

papers.title: Complementary Cauchy Elasticity
papers.abstract: We develop a nonlinear theory of complementary Cauchy elasticity in which the right Cauchy-Green strain is prescribed as a function of the second Piola-Kirchhoff stress, without assuming constitutive invertibility or the existence of a complementary strain-energy function. We introduce the complementary stress-work 1-form and characterize the obstruction to complementary hyperelasticity through the failure of major symmetry of the tangent compliance tensor. For general implicit elasticity, we show that the simultaneous closure of the stress-work and complementary stress-work 1-forms is characterized by the Lagrangian structure of the constitutive manifold. Using the Darboux classification, we obtain local canonical representations of anisotropic and isotropic complementary Cauchy elastic solids, including explicit non-hyperelastic examples. We investigate kinematic and stress constraints, including applications to pentamode solids, and show that internally constrained constitutive relations are naturally formulated on equivalence classes of stresses modulo reactive stresses. We formulate the balance laws and thermodynamics covariantly and establish that covariance of the energy balance directly yields the balance of angular momentum in complementary Cauchy elasticity, unlike in conventional Cauchy elasticity. Finally, we linearize implicit, Cauchy, and complementary Cauchy elasticity about finitely deformed and prestressed configurations and show that nonlinear non-hyperelastic solids may possess hyperelastic linearized responses.

papers.title: gKSM: GPU Memory Deduplication at Driver Layer for Serverless LLM Inference
papers.abstract: In serverless LLM inference, cloud providers commonly locate multiple instances on a single GPU to improve utilization. However, each instance independently maintains its model weights and runtime state, making duplicate GPU memory the primary bottleneck. Memory deduplication is a widely-used technique for eliminating duplicate data in CPU systems, but extending it to GPU memory faces fundamental challenges. Effective GPU memory deduplication must avoid redundant data movement between CPU and GPU while preserving write isolation for shared pages without native copy-on-write (COW) support. This paper presents gKSM, a transparent GPU memory deduplication framework for serverless LLM inference. gKSM addresses these challenges through CPU-GPU collaborative hash management that offloads hash computation to GPU kernels, zero-copy model weight deduplication that eliminates duplication before model weight transfer, and a cross-privilege page fault handler that combines a lightweight kernel hook and CUDA Virtual Memory Management (VMM) remapping in the user space. gKSM also designs a stable page scanning algorithm and a reuse-aware placement policy in cluster scale. Experiments show that gKSM reduces GPU memory usage by 59.8% while maintaining high throughput compared to ServerlessLLM. Under memory constrained workloads, gKSM improves aggregate throughput by 2.15X and supports five instances concurrently. In cluster level simulation, gKSM achieves a service rate of 99.97%, compared to 78.2% for SLInfer and 26.9% for ServerlessLLM.

papers.title: DROD: Dual-Ratio Ordered Dropout for Federated Continual Learning on Heterogeneous Devices
papers.abstract: Federated learning for capacity-heterogeneous clients and federated continual learning are each well studied on their own, but their intersection -- clients holding differently sized models while every client's data stream also drifts over time -- remains underexplored. We study this setting directly, training a ResNet-18 fleet from scratch on Split-CIFAR-100 (10 tasks, class-incremental), and introduce DROD (Dual-Ratio Ordered Dropout), which builds on FjORD's Ordered Dropout by using two independent reduction axes to extract sub-models: a shortcut ratio and a branch ratio. On a shared parameter/FLOP budget ladder, DROD achieves the highest mean accuracy among the heterogeneous-model federated learning strategies we compare. Its advantage over the two strongest baseline geometries persists across every replay-buffer size we test and under ER, DER++, and BiC; under EWC, all three geometries collapse alike.

papers.title: When Semantics Fall Short: Persona-Guided Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Cross-domain sequential recommendation (CDSR) alleviates data sparsity by transferring user behaviors across domains. Recent advances increasingly leverage large language models (LLMs) to bridge domains through global item semantics. However, this paradigm is inherently limited by two issues: I. semantic domain isolation, where item semantics remain domain-specific and hinder transferable modeling, and II. semantic-behavior inconsistency, where local semantic relations are more consistent with behavioral transitions, whereas such consistency often breaks down globally across domains. To this end, we propose PerCDR, an LLM-enhanced CDSR framework that shifts the focus from global semantic bridging to persona-guided behavioral modeling. Specifically, PerCDR leverages LLM-inferred personas to globally guide transferable cross-domain behavioral patterns, while exploiting local semantic relations to enhance intra-domain behavioral modeling, followed by domain preference adaptation for recommendation refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of PerCDR and validate its effectiveness.

papers.title: Self-Trapping and Liouvillian Spectral Transitions in a Dissipative Bose-Hubbard Dimer
papers.abstract: We study the self-trapping transition in dissipative double wells using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization. We find that, similar to the conventional interaction-driven transition from oscillatory dynamics to self-trapping, dissipation alone can also induce self-trapping-like localization in one well. The resulting state, although transient and decaying, persists for a substantial time. At the mean-field level, the interaction- and dissipation-driven transitions are discontinuous and continuous, respectively. When interaction and dissipation both are present, their interplay produces three dynamical regimes: (i) at weak interaction, increasing dissipation drives a transition from oscillations to self-trapping; (ii) at moderate interaction, self-trapping at weak dissipation, oscillatory dynamics at intermediate dissipation, and re-entrant self-trapping at strong dissipation; and (iii) at strong interaction, self-trapping persists but is weakened by dissipation. We connect the transition with the Liouvillian spectrum. It is observed that purely dissipation-driven transition coincides with an exceptional point in the spectra, and a peak in the Liouvillian gap, marking the onset of the quantum-Zeno regime. In the presence of interactions, however, the onset of the Zeno regime is shifted to dissipation strengths larger than that required for the self-trapping transition.

papers.title: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control
papers.abstract: Controllable video generation has recently achieved impressive visual quality, yet existing control paradigms remain poorly suited to embodied navigation. Text prompts are spatially ambiguous, while camera-trajectory control relies on low-level motion specifications that are unintuitive for human users and difficult to manipulate. In this work, we introduce Map2Vid, a novel task that reformulates embodied navigation video generation as a BEV-map-to-video synthesis problem, together with a large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation. By using BEV maps, which provide a visual representation of global scene layout and intended navigation routes, Map2Vid enables human-friendly navigation video generation. To support this task, we construct a dedicated dataset with over 100K navigation sequences across 61 indoor scenes, each paired with egocentric videos, BEV maps, camera trajectories and language instructions. We further develop a unified framework that integrates multiple control signals, together with a curriculum training strategy that progressively weakens non-map inputs, enabling flexible inference under both full conditioning and map-only input. Extensive experiments across multiple foundation generation models demonstrate that controllable navigation video generation via BEV map is a viable and promising direction.

papers.title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
papers.abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone. The proof recovers $C(X)$ from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of $L^p$-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.

papers.title: $Δ(1232)$ isobars and weak-interaction bulk viscosity in neutron-star merger matter
papers.abstract: Binary neutron star mergers probe nuclear matter at densities of a few times nuclear saturation density and temperatures of tens of MeV, conditions under which heavier baryons such as the $Δ(1232)$ isobars may appear. Previous calculations of the bulk viscosity of merger matter have considered nucleonic matter, with and without muons, and hyperonic matter, but not $Δ$ isobars. In this work, we extend these calculations to neutrino-transparent matter in which $Δ$ isobars are present in strong equilibrium. We derive the relativistic matrix elements for the charged-current $Δ\to N$ and $Δ\toΔ'$ transitions, evaluate all electronic and muonic Urca processes over the full phase space using the nucleon width approximation, and include the in-medium $Δ\to Nπ$ width with Pauli blocking. The bulk viscosity is obtained from the coupled linear response of the electron and muon fractions about the finite-temperature flavor equilibrium. We find that the $Δ^-$ takes over the negative charge from the leptons, which raises the proton fraction and opens the nucleonic direct Urca process. Up to about 3~MeV this change in composition, rather than the $Δ$ reactions themselves, controls flavor equilibration. As a consequence, the resonant maximum of the bulk viscosity moves to lower temperatures for all oscillation frequencies we consider, and kHz density oscillations near resonance are damped several times faster than in nucleonic matter. We also show that, for nucleonic matter, the choice of the equilibrium state about which the rates are linearized shifts the resonance temperature by up to a few MeV at high density.

papers.title: AI-Enhanced Radiation Classification in ROS
papers.abstract: This study presents the development of two Robot Operating System (ROS) nodes with a primary focus on differentiating seven radioactive isotopes. The first node, referred to as the model training node, uses a Gradient Boosting classifier to identify and classify these isotopes. The classifier achieved a reported overall accuracy of 95\% on the held-out test dataset. The second node, known as the prediction node, provides classification results when users input data in CSV format. For the practical demonstration, the C12137 radiation detector module was mounted on the Jackal UGV, and an operator approached different radiation sources to collect data. To support future dataset expansion, we also developed a method for converting gamma-spectrum graph images into CSV files. In a separate robotic evaluation across three source locations, 30 of 42 trials were correctly classified (71.43\%). Am-241, Co-60, Cs-137, Na-22, and Ti-44 were correctly classified in all six trials each, whereas Ba-133 and Eu-152 were incorrectly classified in all six trials each. These results show lower accuracy in robotic trials than in the held-out test set.

papers.title: Generalized symmetric pairs, Lie superalgebras, Dirac operators and Kostant constants
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a geometric construction of contragredient Lie superalgebras, with the exceptions of $A(m,n)$ $(m,n>0)$ and $G(3)$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an order 4 automorphism $σ$, the eigenspace decomposition being $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)$. When $\mathfrak{g}(i)$ admits a $\mathfrak{g}(1)$-invariant symplectic structure, $(\mathfrak{g},σ)$ is called a \emph{generalized symmetric pair with symplectic subspace}. In this paper, we classify all such pairs and construct a natural Lie superalgebra structure on $L= L_{\bar{0}}+L_{\bar{1}}$ with $L_{\bar{0}}=\mathfrak{g}(1)$ and $L_{\bar{1}}=\mathfrak{g}(i)$. Furthermore, we investigate the constants arising from the squares of two distinct Dirac operators: $D$ for $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}^{σ^2}+\mathfrak{g}^{-σ^2}$, and $D_s$ for $L=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)$. We prove that the constant $C$ in $D^2$ admits a remarkable factorization \[C=J^*(Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}})\cdot\dim L_{\bar{1}}\cdot h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}},\] where $h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}}$ is the signed dual Coxeter number of $L$ and $J^*(Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}})$ is a mapped Casimir constant of its even part. This formula reveals an unexpected unification of symmetric space geometry and Lie superalgebra invariants. Finally, we prove that the Kostant constant $\mathrm{K_s} = \left.Ω_{L_{\bar{0}}}\right|_{L_{\bar{1}}}=\frac{1}{2}$ is universal for all contragredient Lie superalgebras with non-degenerate Killing form, which implies that the constant $C_s$ in $D_s^2$ satisfies $C_s=\frac{1}{16}\dim L_{\bar{0}}$. We then establish a bijection between such superalgebras and solutions of the superadmissibility index equations $E_s^{I\!I} =\frac{1}{2}, E_s^I = \frac{1}{2}$, recovering the classification from an invariant-theoretic perspective.

papers.title: An inclusion coupling of prefix laws and the Chan-Pak rank inequality for all finite posets
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a finite poset, let $x\in P$, and let $N_k$ count its linear extensions in which $x$ occupies position $k$. We prove Chan and Pak's conjecture that, for all integers $a,h\ge1$, \[ (a+h-1)N_{a+h-1}N_a\ \ge\ (a-1)N_{a-1}N_{a+h}+hN_aN_{a+h}. \] The key result is an inclusion coupling of the laws of the set of elements preceding $x$, conditional on consecutive positions of $x$. We construct reversible exchange chains on the corresponding layers of order ideals and couple their generators so that the two prefix sets remain nested. Fishburn's correlation inequality gives monotonicity of endpoint probabilities; their unit total masses provide the rate bounds needed for the coupling. A stationary distribution of the coupled chain then has the required marginals. Normalized cover observables yield a four-term nonnegative certificate for the case $h=1$, and the general case follows by telescoping. The argument applies at every width and gives a proof of Stanley's log-concavity inequality with Fishburn's inequality as its sole external inequality.

papers.title: Covering finite fields by translates of multiplicative subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $G_d$ be the subgroup of index $d>1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and put $G_d^0=G_d\cup\{0\}$. For a covering $A+G_d^0=\mathbb{F}_q$ with $\#A=s$, we prove $q\le d^{8s/d}$ by shifting the roots of a Bonferroni polynomial. Although a uniform bound in $s$ alone must allow exponential growth, our estimate confines such growth to bounded indices and gives polynomial bounds when $s/d$ is bounded. A cubic specialization gives bounds of degree at most eight for $s\le2d$. For shift sets of logarithmic size, higher moment estimates give a uniform covering-probability formula, including the critical window. Together with the index restriction, this determines the covering indices of almost every shift set of size $\lceil k\log q\rceil$ for each fixed integer $k\ge2$. A subfield construction attains the order of the uniform restriction on the index. We determine its covering number exactly and prove minimality under subgroup inclusion. We also characterize equality in the elementary counting bound by subfield cosets. Fixing a subfield as the shift set in a quadratic extension leads to a sharper projection bound, attained by an infinite family with unique representations outside the shift subfield.

papers.title: The Streets--Tian conjecture on compact homogeneous quotients
papers.abstract: A Hermitian-symplectic metric is a Hermitian metric whose Kähler form is given by the $(1,1)$-part of a closed $2$-form. Streets-Tian Conjecture states that a compact complex manifold admitting a Hermitian-symplectic metric must be Kählerian (i.e., admitting a Kähler metric). We study Hermitian-symplectic metrics on homogeneous complex manifolds with compact isotropy, and on their compact discrete quotients. If the transitive group is connected and unimodular, we show that an invariant Hermitian-symplectic form gives an invariant Kähler metric, with no lattice assumption. By averaging, the same conclusion holds for compact quotients, even if the initial metric has no invariant lift. The proof uses the top exterior power of a Hermitian-symplectic form to bound the volume functional on an invariant Aeppli slice. Applying this bound to midpoint metrics gives a uniform trace estimate. From this, volume maximization produces a balanced metric in the slice, which is also pluriclosed and hence Kähler. We also describe the resulting Kähler representative and give examples showing the role of the closed lift.

papers.title: Local Approximation of $A$-Harmonic Functions and the Super-Localization Conjecture
papers.abstract: We consider the local energy approximation of $A$-harmonic functions on concentric cubes with a fixed size ratio in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, for bounded, symmetric, uniformly elliptic diffusion tensors~$A$. We give a short proof of the Kolmogorov $n$-width decay rate $\exp(-cn^{1/(d-1)})$ conjectured by Ma [Found.\ Comput.\ Math.\ 26 (2026), 1699--1758], where $n$ denotes the approximation dimension. We apply this result to numerical homogenization, improving local approximation estimates for multiscale spectral generalized finite element methods and proving the conjectured local super-localization rate of Hauck and Peterseim [Math.\ Comp.\ 92 (2023), 981--1003] for interior Cartesian patches.

papers.title: AgentLens: Framework-Aware Characterization and Resource Control for Heterogeneous LLM Agents
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed on shared hosts, yet their host-side resource demands remain poorly understood, limiting effective resource coordination. We present AgentLens, which combines a cross-framework workload characterization with a framework-aware resource controller for co-located agents. Across 10 frameworks and 11 matched coding tasks, we find that framework orchestration strongly shapes resource demand: framework identity explains 52.95% of peak RSS variance, compared with 4.22% for task identity, while execve events per tool call differ by 39x between MetaGPT and CAMEL. Resource dimensions are not interchangeable: peak RSS and subprocess count have a Spearman correlation of 0.13. Static budgets and framework-agnostic policies miss these structural differences and the alternation between API waiting and tool execution. AgentLens combines offline framework fingerprints with online execution-phase signals to coordinate memory through cgroup v2, without modifying framework internals. In trace-driven replay across three co-location pairs at a memory budget of 90% of aggregate peak demand, AgentLens keeps the protected worker's P95 allocation latency at 5.7-7.1 ms, improving on static allocation by 2.1-2.6x.

papers.title: Classification of Isometric Immersions of Spherical and HCMU Footballs into $\E^{3}$
papers.abstract: We study global isometric immersions of rotational metrics with two conical ends into Euclidean three-space. For a metric $g=\mathrm{d}u^2+f(u)^2\mathrm{d}θ^2$ of positive Gauss curvature, we prove that vanishing endpoint traces of the weighted mixed shape coefficient $f^2b$ force every smooth isometric immersion to be rotational. The resulting congruence classes are parametrized by an integer angular covering degree bounded below by the two cone-angle parameters. The proof combines a scalar elliptic equation derived from the Gauss--Codazzi system, the maximum principle, and a global angular closing condition. For spherical footballs, isolated-singularity theory and a direct estimate in coordinates conformal for the second fundamental form establish the trace condition for every smooth immersion of the regular part. We also classify all rotational isometric immersions of HCMU footballs, including those whose curvature changes sign. When the minimum curvature is nonnegative, this classification exhausts the immersions satisfying the trace condition, and hence all immersions admitting a $C^2$ polar extension at both tips.

papers.title: Noise-Awareness in Quantum Software Testing: An Empirical Landscape Analysis
papers.abstract: Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) hardware has transformed quantum computing into a practical experimental platform while introducing fundamental challenges associated with hardware noise, decoherence, and probabilistic execution. Although quantum software testing (QST) has rapidly emerged as an active research area, it remains unclear to what extent existing testing methodologies explicitly engage with noisy and hardware-constrained execution environments. This paper presents a systematic empirical landscape analysis of noise-awareness in QST research through a deterministic, taxonomy-guided analytical framework applied to 61 papers published between 2018 and 2025 across eight testing paradigms, contrasting how contributions are framed with how they are evaluated. Among the analyzed papers, 47 (77.0%) are noise-oblivious and only 14 (23.0%) explicitly engage with noise-related execution concerns, while only 11 (18.0%) report evaluation on physical hardware or a noisy simulator. Test generation, the largest paradigm, exhibits a noise-awareness rate of only 14.3%, and debugging and repair 18.2%; coverage-based, metamorphic, and differential testing contain no noise-aware contributions. Noise-aware methodologies emerged late and remain outnumbered in all analyzed years. Framing and evaluation are strongly associated (odds ratio 40.5, p < 0.001) yet diverge for individual papers: 5 of the 14 noise-aware papers evaluate only on ideal simulators. Inferential statistical tests are reported in only 16.4% of papers. The classification framework was validated against a blinded, human-coded reference sample, achieving almost perfect inter-rater agreement on testing-technique classification and substantial agreement on noise-awareness.
